πάγη.definition: anything that fixes or fastens; metaph., trap, snare, A.Ag.822; of the beacons of Nauplius, S.Fr.435

πάγκρεας.definition: sweetbread, pancreas; nickname given by Timo to the sceptic Pyrrho, Timo31

πᾶγος.definition: = Lat. pagus, district, Plu.Num.16, PGen.54.33 , etc

παιδέρως.definition: holm-oak, Quercus Ilex, Paus.2.10.6; chervil, Anthriscus cerefolium, Plin.HN19.170

παῖς.definition: in relation to Descent, child, whether son, Il.2.205,609, al. : pl., Th.1.4, etc.; or daughter, Il.1.20,443, 3.175; Pl.Lg.788a; opp. Berl.Sitzb.1927.7 ; of an adopted son, Il.9.494; 20.308, cf. Pi.N.7.100, Inscr.Cypr.…

πάλαξις.definition: laying on of a preliminary coat of paint, priming, IG42.109 iii 111, 117

πάλσις.definition: rapid motion, vibration, Porph; brandishing, EM394.56; palpitation, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.247

πανθήρα.definition: a birdcatcher's whole catch, Ulp. in Dig.19.1.11.18; cf. Lat. panthera, = rete aucupale, Gloss

πανόψιος.definition: all-seen, in the sight of all; all-seeing, Nonn.D.14.169

πάνσυρτος.definition: swept together from every side, a life of accumulated woe, S.El.851

πανσχήμων.definition: gen. of every, i.e. of indeterminate, form, Theol.Ar.8, cf. Iamb.in Nic.p.57 P

παντελής.definition: all-complete, absolute; perfect, Philol. ap. Stob.1Prooem.3, cf. Dam.Pr.195

παός.definition: Dor. for in aor. Pass., become a Alc.Supp.23.6

παπίας.definition: janitor or keeper of the Palace, Tz.H.3.839

παράβολος.definition: with a side-meaning, deceitful, h.Merc.56; exposing oneself or what belongs to one: hence

παράδειξις.definition: proof, establishment of a fact; indication, Iamb.Comm.Math.p.8 F

παρακοή.definition: that which has been heard imperfectly; misunderstanding, Gal.4.764, 8.629

πάραλος.definition: by or near the sea, S.Aj.413; generally, concerned with the sea, naval, Hdt.7.161

πάραμμα.definition: thong for carrying burdens, in Lat. form paramma , Edict.Diocl.10.3

παράψογος.definition: incidental censure, Rhet. word used by Evenus of Paros. Pl.Phdr.267a

πάρδαλος.definition: v.l. for in Ael.NA1.31; a gregarious bird, perh. the plover, Arist.HA617b6

πάρδος.definition: later form of Ael.NA1.31; Lat. pardus, the male of the panthera, Plin.HN8.63

παρειάς.definition: bandage for the cheek, Heliod. ap; cheek, A.R.4.172 , Heliod. l.c

παρέκτοπος.definition: somewhat out of the way, Gloss

παρέκτωρ.definition: provider, Ramsay Studies in the Eastern Roman Provinces p.128

πάρηβος.definition: past one's prime, APl.4.289; past boyhood, Ph.2.59

παρήλιος.definition: parhelion, mock sun, Arist.Mete.372a16; Adj. beside the sun, Ptol.Tetr.100

παρηορία.definition: in pl., side-traces, by which the; in pl., outlying reaches of a river, Arat.600

πάρμη.definition: light shield, buckler, Lat. parma, Plb.6.22.1, D.H.2.71, etc

πάροικος.definition: dwelling beside or near, neighbouring, c; war with neighbours, Hdt.7.235

παρόρθιος.definition: tolerably straight, not quite straight, Apollod.Poliorc.146.7, 154.4:—also ib.143.11

πάρορνις.definition: having ill omens, ill- omened voyages, A.Eu.770

πάρουρος.definition: one who keeps watch beside, v.l. in Od.11.489; beside the tail, Ptol.Alm.8.1, al

πάρυδρος.definition: living near water, of the halcyon, Arist.HA593b8; of water-plants, Thphr.HP4.12.4

πάρωρος.definition: out of season, untimely; beyond the proper time, too old for . . , Epicur.Ep.3p.59U

παρωτίς.definition: tumour of the parotid gland; lobe of the ear, Lyc.1402

πάσσαλος.definition: Att. Ep. gen. (v; from the like ness of form

πάσσον.definition: = Lat. vinum passum, raisin wine, Plb.6.11a.4

πάσσων.definition: gen. Ep. Comp. of thicker, stouter, Od.6.230, cf. 8.20; of a woman, 18.195

παστός.definition: sprinkled with salt, salted; powder, Hp.Loc.Hom.13

πάσχα.definition: indecl., the Hebrew Passover (from pāsaḥ; paschal supper, Ev.Matt.26.17, 19,al

πατήρ.definition: gen. and dat. in Ep. and; respectful mode of addressing persons older than oneself, Od.7.28,48,8.145, cf. POxy. 1296.15 , etc.; in addressing an elder brother, UPZ65.3

πάτρα.definition: Ion. and Ep. fatherland; fatherhood, descent from a common father, Il.13.354 ; by hereditary descent, IGRom.4.1730 : hence

πατταλίας.definition: two-year-old stag or buck, when the horns are still mere pegs or 'dags', brocket or pricket, Arist.HA611a34

παῦς.definition: in nom. sg., = Kretschmer Griech. Vaseninschr. p.188

πάχετος.definition: = thick, massive, twice in; tight, of a knot or ligature, Hp.Mul.2.110: neut. as Adv., Id.Cord.6

πέδη.definition: fetter: in pl., shackles; anklet, bangle, Ar.Fr.320.11, Philem.81, Luc.Lex.9

πεδητής.definition: Dor. one who fetters: metaph., hinderer, AP9.756

πεδήτης.definition: Pass., one fettered, prisoner; at Samos, building in which certain fetters were kept, Plu.2.303e

πεδίον.definition: plain, in Hom. mostly sg; metaph., of the sea, A.Fr.150; Ion Trag.60; Tim.Pers.89

πέδων.definition: one in fetters, of a slave, Ar.Fr.837

πέζα.definition: said to be Dor. and Arc. for; metaph., bottom, end of a body, on the pole at the far end, Il.24.272

πεζότης.definition: the being furnished with feet, Simp.in Cat.100.16

πεῖνα.definition: Ion. hunger, famine; metaph., hunger or longing for a thing, Pl.Phlb.52a

πεῖσμα.definition: ship's cable, usu. the stern-; generally, rope, Od.10.167; boat-rope, painter, Theophil.6

πέλασις.definition: approach, Iamb.Comm.Math.8, Procl.in Prm.p.513 S.; Stoic.2.119

πέλεια.definition: dove or pigeon, esp. wild rock-; prophetic priestesses at Dodona, Paus.7.21.2, 10.12.10; cf. sq. II and

πελειάς.definition: = foreg. I, mostly in pl; an Indian fruit-pigeon, Crocopus chlorogaster, Ael.NA16.2

πέλλα.definition: Ion. wooden bowl, milk-pail; drinking-cup, Hippon.39

πέλτης.definition: the Nile-fish salted, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.3.121b

πέλτον.definition: platform for a sarcophagus, Supp.Epigr.6.307, 428, 434 ; cf

πέλωρ.definition: portent, prodigy, monster, Ep. Noun, only nom. and acc., in early writers always of living beings, mostly in bad sense, as of the Cyclops, Od.9.428: of Scylla, 12.87; of the serpent Python, h.Ap.374; of a dolphin, ib.…

πέμπτος.definition: fifth : with four others; the fifth day, Hes.Op.802, 803, Ar.Nu.1131

πένης.definition: one who works for his living; as Adj., E.El.1139: c. neut., ib.372: c. gen., poor in money, ib.38; Pl.Ep.332c: Luc.Apol.11: Comp. X.Ath.1.13: Sup. D.21.123

πενθερός.definition: generally, connexion by marriage, e.g. brother-in- law, Id.El.1286; also, = son-in-law, S.Fr.305

πενία.definition: Ion. poverty, need; lack, need, Plot.2.4.16

πέπειρα.definition: rare fem. of (formed on analogy of; of things, soft, pulpy, Hp.VC11 : metaph., S.Tr.728

πέπειρος.definition: ripe, of fruit, Thphr.CP3.6.9; metaph., of persons, mild, D.H.9.49

πέπερι.definition: pepper, Piper nigrum, Antiph.277; long pepper, Piper officinarum, Thphr.HP9.20.1, Dsc.2.159. .)

πεπλίς.definition: wild purslane, Euphorbia Peplis, Dsc.4.168:—also in Dim. form Hp.Acut.23, Gal.12.97

πέπων.definition: gen. Comp. and Sup; of abscesses, ripe, ready to suppurate, Hermipp.30

πέρα.definition: Adv. beyond, further; c. gen., further than, Lex ap.D.23.44; Arist.Pol.1319b14, cf. Pl.Ti.29d

περαίας.definition: a kind of mullet found beyond, i. e. at a distance from, the bank, opp. Arist.HA591a23

περίακτος.definition: turning on a centre or pivot; a winding road, Anon.Hist. p.819 J

περίαλλος.definition: before all others: Adv. before; as Adj., superlative, AP5.131

περίγειος.definition: surrounding the earth, opp; of the earth, opp. etc., Cat.Cod.Astr.8.252

περιδορά.definition: removal of skin all round, Aët.15.8, Paul.Aeg.6.39

περίθριξ.definition: the first growth of hair before it is cut, Call.Fr. anon.56

περίισος.definition: more than equal, coined as etym. of Theol.Ar.13

περίκομος.definition: covered all over with leaves, Thphr.HP3.8.4,al

περικράνιος.definition: round the skull, skull-; = cernicale, Gloss

περινομή.definition: distribution in regular order; procession round a place, Men.894

περίοδος.definition: one who goes the rounds, patrol, Aen.Tact.22.3, al., Rev.Arch.1911.424

περίοπτος.definition: to be seen all round, in a commanding; Subst. belvederes, Plu.Luc.39

περιρρυής.definition: falling down all round, gloss on Pius ap. Orum in EM664.39

περιφαής.definition: gleaming all round, metri gr.] Opp.H.2.6

περίφορος.definition: carried about by passing impulse; Subst. f.l. for or in Luc.Astr.5

περιφυής.definition: growing round about, growing close to the ground, v.l. for in Dsc.4.103

περίχθων.definition: gen. round about the earth, AP9.778 , dub. in Orph.Fr.285.57

πεσσός.definition: Att. heterocl. pl. S.Fr.429; the board on which the game was played, since the pieces were placed on five lines, S.Fr.429

πέτευρον.definition: roosting-perch for fowls, Ar.Fr.839; generally, pole, spar, plank, Lyc.884

πέτρα.definition: Ion. and Ep. rock; freq. of cliffs, ledges, etc. by the sea, Od.3.293, cf. 4.501, etc.; free from rocks, of a beach, 5.443; . . Il.15.618, etc.; Pi.P.10.52; also, rocky peak or ridge, Il.9.15, etc.; 16.35, etc.; Corin…

πέτρινος.definition: changed into rock, of Niobe, Tz.H.4.715; a Celtic manoeuvre, Arr.Tact.37.4

πέψις.definition: Ion. softening, ripening; of fruit, Id.Mete.380a11, cf. Thphr.HP1.12.2, 5.1.3

πηδόν.definition: blade of an oar: hence generally, oar; in pl. = Arat.155

πηδός.definition: tree whose timber was used for axles, etc., Thphr.HP5.7.6; perh. = ; cf

πήκασμα.definition: f.l., perh. for in pl., trappings for horses, Hippiatr.14

πηκτίς.definition: shepherd's pipe, Pan's pipes, APl.4.244 ; AP9.586 , cf. Procop.Gaz.p.137 B

πήνη.definition: thread on the bobbin in the shuttle, woof, and; bobbin, spool, AP6.160

πῆξις.definition: Ion. fixing, putting; Astrol., fixing, Vett.Val.24.18, cf. Cat.Cod.Astr.2.196

πηρίνα.definition: = Gal.19.130 ; also cited from Hp.Haem. and Fist., = ibid

πῆρος.definition: Aeol. loss of strength, dotage, Alc.98

πίασμα.definition: that which makes fat, of a river, bringing fatness and riches to . . , A.Pers.806

πιθίας.definition: jar-shaped comet, Seneca QN1.14, Phlp.in Mete.92.34:—written Procl.Par.Ptol.131

πιμεντάριος.definition: spicer, apothecary, Olymp.in Grg.p.362 J., al., cj. for in Aët.15.29. mentarius.)

πινίκιος.definition: of the = Peripl.M.Rubr.35: pearl produced by the ib.36, 59

πῖνον.definition: liquor made from barley, beer, Arist.Fr.106, cj. in Atti della reale Accad. di Archeologia di Napoli11.41

πίνος.definition: dirt, filth, in clothes or hair, S.OC1259; patina on bronze statues, Plu.2.395b: hence, metaph. of style, D.H.Dem.5, cf.39, Comp.11, al

πῖος.definition: poet. form of Epich.136; Orph.A.506: hence v

πιότης.definition: fattiness, Hp.Aër.21, cf; metaph., wealth, prosperity, Ph.1.299, Eust.1146.10

πιόφυλλος.definition: with oily leaves, of the olive, etc., Alex.Aphr.in Top.118.31

πῖπος.definition: v.l. for in Arist.HA609a30, 617a28; a young piping bird, cj. for in Ath.9.368f

πιπώ.definition: woodpecker, Picus major and minor, Arist.HA593a4, al. , Lyc.476, Nic.Fr.54, prob. in Antim.Col.4P

πῖσος.definition: old Ep. Noun, only in pl., meadows, Il.20.9, cf. Call.Fr.anon.57, A.R.1.1266

πιστότης.definition: good faith, honesty, Hdt.7.52; in order to produce conviction in you, And.1.25

πίτυρον.definition: husks of corn, bran, in sg; bran-like eruption on the skin, esp. the head, scurf, dandruff, Dsc.1.30

πίων.definition: neut. gen. (irreg. fem; metaph., of soil, rich, etc., Il.23.832, 16.437, etc.; rich crops, 12.283; Pi.P.4.56

πλακοῦς.definition: voc. Theodos.Can.p.3; the seed of the mallow, which seeds children call cheeses, Phan.Hist.29, Gal.10.113

πλάσις.definition: moulding, conformation; training of the voice, Plu.Cic.4

πλάσμα.definition: anything formed or moulded, image; the body, as fashioned by the Creator, PMag.Par.1.212

πλαταμών.definition: any broad flat body or; flat beach, in pl., AP7.404 , v.l. in Dsc.4.73

πλάτας.definition: also platform on which tombs were placed, TAM2.438 , CIG2825, al. ; cf

πλατύτης.definition: breadth, width, of the liver; breadth of pronunciation, Demetr.Eloc.177

πλίκιον.definition: a kind of cake, Chrysipp.Tyan. ap. Ath.14.647c

πλοχμός.definition: like mostly in pl., locks, braids; tentacles of the polypus, AP9.10
