παρασφάλλω.definition: aor. , cause to glance off to the side, of an arrow, Il.8.311; foil one of . . , Pi.N.11.31; Opp.H.3.200:—Pass., err, be deceived, Critias6.13; . . having wandered from it, Pl.Epin.976b, cf. Procl.in Prm.p.548 S.; Com…

παρατεκταίνομαι.definition: Med., prop. of timber, work into; later in Act., build besides, Plu.Pomp.40

παρατίθημι.definition: Dor. and poet. (late forms from; freq. of meals, set before, serve up, Il.23.810, cf. 9.90 ; Od.1.192; 20.260; 4.66; Il.18.408; 11.779, cf. Od.9.517 ; 5.92: c. gen., Hdt.4.73, cf. 1.119 ; X.An.4.5.31; the serving-men,…

παρατρέπω.definition: aor. 2 Hes.Th.103:—Med. (v; turn one from his opinion, change his mind, Hes.Th.103; A.R.3.902:—Med., Theoc.22.151:— Pass., Pl.Lg.885d; ib.906e

παρατρέχω.definition: fut. Com.Adesp.555: aor; accompany, c. dat., Eun.VSp.499B

παρατροπέω.definition: = why tell me this, trying to lead me astray, to mislead me? Od.4.4.65, cf. A.R.3.946

παρατυγχάνω.definition: abs., happen to be present, Hdt.1.59, 6.108; of things, offer, present itself, Hp.Art.38; Th.4.19; Id.8.11; Pl.R.474a

παραυδάω.definition: console, encourage; c. acc. rei, speak lightly of, make light of, 11.488

παραύξω.definition: lengthen a syllable metrically, D.H.Comp.11, cf. 15; intr., wax, Gem.6.39

παραφαίνω.definition: poet. show beside or by; produce, the form of oath, Ar.Lys.183

παράφημι.definition: poet. and speak gently to; freq. with collat. notion of deceit, speak deceitfully or insincerely, Pi.O.7.66, P.9.43:—Med., beguiling him, Id.N.5.32

παραφθάνω.definition: aor. 2 part. Act. and Med. :—overtake, outstrip, . . Il.22.197; 10.346; 23.515; of a horse, win a race, Paus.5.8.8, cf. Hld.4.4

παραφρίζω.definition: foam at the side, of the mouth, Nic.Al.223

παραφυής.definition: growing beside, of extra fingers, Paul.Aeg.6.43: = Arist.Rh.1356a25

παραφωνή.definition: pseudo-sound, as it were the reflexion or image of a sound in the ear, Epicurei ap.Ael. in Pl.Ti

παράφωνος.definition: sounding beside; sounds midway between consonances and dissonances, e.g. the tritone, Gaud.Harm.8

παραχαλάω.definition: open a passage for; intr., of a ship, let in water, leak, Ar.Eq.434

παραψαύω.definition: pf. S.E.M.7.116:—touch gently; metaph., touch lightly or slightly on a subject, S.E.l.c. :—Pass., . . Hp.Morb.4.44

παραψάω.definition: brush sideways, smoothed; wipe, Zos.Alch.p.234 B

παραψήχω.definition: rub at the side, Ael.NA9.16; smooth down, Plu.2.641e

παρεγγύη.definition: = allegatio, insinuatio, Gloss; Dor. deposit paid by a contractor, IG42.109 ii 152

παρέγχυμα.definition: anything poured in beside, name given by Erasistratus to the peculiar substance of the lungs, liver, kidneys, and spleen, as if formed separately by the veins that run into them, the word being used of the muscular fl…

παρέζομαι.definition: sit beside, Thgn.563; in Hom. we find only forms that prob. belong to an aor. viz. Il.1.407; ib.557; . . 5.889, cf. Od.4.738, 20.334

παρείκω.definition: aor. 2 , give way; relax, let fall, Clearch.25

πάρειμι.definition: to be by or near one, c. dat., Od.5.105; 4.640; Antipho4.1.7; S.Ph.1056; to be his guest, Ar.Av.131

παρεκθέω.definition: run past, c. acc. loci, A.R.1.592: abs., penetrate, Aret.CD2.13

παρεκλέγω.definition: collect covertly, embezzle the; of birds, collect food here and there, Ael.NA8.25, cf.17.16

παρεκλύω.definition: relieve from, Sor.2.11; Pass., to be cut off from, unreceptive of, Phld.Herc.1251.18

παρεκπροφεύγω.definition: flee forth from, elude one's grasp, Il.23.314

παρεκρέω.definition: aor. 2 inf. run out at the side, Dsc.Eup.1.235

παρελαύνω.definition: c. acc. pers., drive past, overtake another, ib.638; but drive on to Trachis, Hes.Sc.353; also X.An.1.2.16, 3.4.46

παρέλκω.definition: fut. LXXSi.29.8 : aor; lead alongside, as a led horse, Hdt.3.102:—Med., Harp.s.v. to be towed from the bank, Hdt.2.96

παρελπίζω.definition: to be disappointed in one's hopes of, Phld.Lib.p.8 O

παρεμφέρω.definition: to be somewhat like, Asclep. ap; Pass., to be brought in besides, Vett. Val.246.15

παρεξάγω.definition: lead past, c. acc. loci, v.l. in

παρεξελαύνω.definition: drive past, pass; ride alongside of, Id.Phil.10, cf. Pyrrh.16

παρεξέρχομαι.definition: Med. with aor. and pf. Act.: aor; c. gen., go aside from the truth, Pl.Phlb.66b

παρερύω.definition: Ion. only aor. Act. and Pass., draw along the side, Hdt.7.36. II. draw on one side, the mouth was distorted

παρέρχομαι.definition: of Time, pass, Hdt.2.86; Aeschin.3.69; time past, E.Fr.1028 ; the past season, S.Tr.69; wanderings now gone by, Id.OC1397; Pl.Phdr.231b, X.An.4.3.2; Pl.Prt.310a; in time past, of old, X.Cyr.8.8.20, etc. ; past events,…

παρευνάζομαι.definition: lie beside, Od.22.37, cf. Poll.5.41:—later Act., Nonn.D.10.200, 25.17

παρέχω.definition: of natural objects, yield, produce, Od.19.113; Il.23.835; of incorporeal things, afford, cause, 3.354, Od.18.133, 20.8; Alc.88; Pi.P.9.23; Id.N.6.33; Id.O.6.102; A.Pers.322; S.OT53, 1306 ; Id.OC1498 , Tr.708; Hdt.1.86…

παρηβάω.definition: pf. Th.2.44:—to be past one's prime; metaph., lose strength, Luc.Lex.13

παρήκω.definition: to have come alongside: hence, lie beside; pass in any direction, S.Aj.742

πάρημαι.definition: used as pf. Pass. of to be seated; abs., sit by or near, Il.9.311, cf. Od.19.209; of the vultures of Tityos, 11.578

παρθένευμα.definition: in pl., pursuits or amusements; child of an unmarried woman, ib.1472

παριαύω.definition: sleep beside or with, Il.9.336, cf. A.R.1.806; in tmesi, Il.9.470, Od.14.21

παρίζω.definition: Aeol. sit beside; causal, seat beside, Id.5.20: aor.1, Il.23.359:—hence Med. in intr. sense, seat oneself or sit beside, Hdt.7.18, 8.58, cj. in Bion2.22; cf

παρίημι.definition: fut. Hdt.7.161, S.Ant.1193: aor. 1; pass unnoticed, disregard, Pi.P.1.86, Hdt.1.14, A.Ag.291, Ch.925, 1032, S.Ant.1193, etc.; . . Id.OC363:—Pass., Id.El.545; D.21.105: c. inf., omit to do, Pl.Phdr.235e, cf. PCair.Zen.…

παρίκω.definition: to be past, of Time, Pi.P.6.43: pf. part., IG12.109.13 , unless pf. of

παρισόω.definition: Pass. .2), make oneself equal to, measure oneself against, Hdt.4.166, Theoc.18.25

παρίστημι.definition: cause to stand, place beside, Plb.3.72.9, cf. 3.113.8; having brought his arms into view, D.18.175; set one near a thing to guard it, v.l. in Id.49.35; Anatolian Studies p.204

παρίσχω.definition: = hold in readiness, Ep. inf. Il.4.229; present, offer, 9.638, Pi.P.8.76; provide, IG7.3073.10 , SIG 245 Gi46

παρίσωσις.definition: Rhet., even balancing of the; equalization, Iamb.Myst.1.9

παροιμία.definition: figure, comparison, Ev.Jo.10.6,al; digression, incidental remark, Herod.2.61, Hsch., Phot

παροινέω.definition: in the augm. tenses with double augm., impf; trans., treat with drunken violence, PSIl. c. :—Pass., to be so treated, D.19.198; Id.54.5

παροίχομαι.definition: of Time, to be past 10.252; the by-gone night, Hdt.1.209,9.58; Id.2.14; Id.8.72; men of by- gone times, Pi.N.6.29 ; Id.I.8.12; X.HG1.4.17; the past, IG12.90.15, Hdt.7.120, cf. X.An.2.4.1; also, the aforesaid, Hp.Fract…

παροράω.definition: aor. : aor. Pass; look past, i.e. overlook a thing, Arist.HA602b3 , Macho ap.Ath.6.244d, etc

παροτρύνω.definition: urge on, c. inf; Medic., displace the uterus, Hp.Mul.2.138

παροχλέω.definition: trouble besides, Arist.Ath.16.7; move as with a lever, dislodge, AP9.204

πάρυγρος.definition: somewhat wet, Man.1.87; plying waterside trades, Vett. Val.2.6

παρυλίζω.definition: make dykes with brushwood, BGU14 iii 1,9 :— hence Subst. ib.13

παρυφιζάνω.definition: to be a concomitant, of symptoms in disease, Sever.Clyst.p.3 D

πασιάναξ.definition: universal king, Orac. ap. Phleg.1.6 J.: applied to the ruler of the dead, and hence to the dead, Tab. Defix.Aud.43, 44

πασσαλεύω.definition: Att. peg, pin, or fasten to; drive in like a peg or bolt, . . A.Pr.65

πάσσω.definition: Att. Ar.Nu.912: fut. Crates; besprinkle, . . Crates Com. l. c., cf. Thphr.Char.9.2; Ar.Nu.912, 1330

πάσχω.definition: Il.20.297, etc. : impf. 17.375, etc; to have something happen to one, to be or come to be in a state or case, Pl.Smp.174e; Ar.Eq.846, cf. V.946; see that it be not with you as with the horse in the fable, Arist.Rh.139…

πατάσσω.definition: Ep. impf. Il.7.216: fut; intr. in Hom., beat, knock, Il.7.216; 23.370; 13.282, cf. Arr.Cyn.15

πατέομαι.definition: Hdt.2.47, Call.Fr.437, Agathocl.Fr.Hist.6, etc. : fut. A.Th.1041: aor. Ep. also : plpf. Il.24.642, elsewh. in Hom. only aor.:—eat, c. acc., Il.1.464, etc. ; 21.76; also, of drink, Hes.Th.642; Nic.Al.312: more freq. c.…

πατέω.definition: Delph. Plu.2.292e; Aeol; trans., tread on, tread, Sapph. l. c.; A.Ag.957; Id.Ch.732; holy ground, S.OC37; tread grapes, Hybrias ; LXXNe.13.15, cf. Apoc.19.15, Ruf. ap. Orib.5.12.1; also, thresh corn, PFlor. 150.5 ; PO…

πάτημα.definition: that which is trodden : refuse; being trodden on, Aret.SD2.12

παύω.definition: causal, make to end; c. acc. only, bring to an end, check, sts. of persons, Il.21.314, cf. S.Ant.963 , Ar.Eq.330; stop or silence by death, Od.20.274, S.OT397:—Pass. and Med., take one's rest, Il.24.17, cf. Hdt.9.52, …

παφλάζω.definition: Aeol. Alc.Supp.25.4 (p.28; metaph., splutter, bluster, of Cleon , Ar.Pax314, Eq.919; Timocl.15.3

πάχνη.definition: hoar-frost, rime (defined as; metaph., the mould and frost of age, descriptive of an old man's grey hair, Com.Adesp.650a, cf. 381; clotted blood of the eaten children, A.Ag.1512

παχνόω.definition: congeal, solidify, Plu.2.396b:—Pass., ib.736a; to be covered with rime, Gp.12.17.1

παχύνω.definition: pf. Pass. Arist.Mu.394a28; thicken, strengthen, Porph.Abst.1.38

πάχυσμα.definition: thickening, Aët.1.59; metaph., Procl.in Cra.p.101 P

πεδάω.definition: Ep. 3sg. Od.4.380: Ep. and Ion. impf; shackle, trammel, Il.13.435; 23.585, cf. Pi.P.6.32, N.5.26; Id.Pae.6.86; Od.13.168; of sleep, 23.17; S.Aj.676; esp. of a deity or fate overruling a mortal's will, c. acc. pers., I…

πεζοβόας.definition: Dor. for one who responds to the battle-cry on foot, foot-soldier, Pi.N.9.34

πείθω.definition: persuade, impf. Il.22.91, etc.; Ep. and; as if from Hom. has fut. Od.21.369 : aor. part. Il.4.398 , cf. Hes.Op.359, 671, Pi.P.4.109, A.Ch.618 , Lyc.735; redupl. aor. subj. trans., Il.22.223:—also Aeol. part. Alc.Supp.…

πεινάω.definition: forms in contr. into not (as in; c. gen., hunger after, Od.20.137

πειράζω.definition: used by early authors only in pres; c. inf., attempt to do, Plb.2.6.9, LXXJd.6.39, Act.Ap.16.7, 24.6; attempt a thing, Luc.Trag.149, cf. S.E.M.1.40; make trial of, Anacreont.31.24: abs., make an attempt, Plb.Fr.195

πειράω.definition: c. gen. pers., make trial of one, for the purpose of persuading, Il.9.345, cf. 24.433; of things, A.R.3.1249: in hostile sense, make an attempt on, Il.12.301, Od.6.134; . . Hdt.6.82; Th.1.61; Id.4.70; Id.7.38; Pi.N.5.30

πειρητίζω.definition: Ep. form of only pres. and impf; c. gen. pers., make trial of, . . Od.14.459; . . . . 15.304; . ., Il.7.235

πείρω.definition: aor. 1 Ep. Il.7.317, etc. :—Pass; metaph., cleaving a way through, Il.24.8, Od.8.183; clave her way [through the sea], 2.434: abs. in the same sense, A.R.2.326,398

πεκτέω.definition: shear, clip, . . Ar.Av.714:—Pass., to be shorn, metaph., of persons, Id.Lys.685

πέκω.definition: Ep. 2pl. pres. imper. Od.18.316 (metri; shear, Hes.Op.775, cf. Theoc.5.98, Ael.NA1.38:—Med., have their wool shorn, Theoc.28.13; Simon.13 :—Pass., Ar.l.c.; Eust.531.5

πελαγίζω.definition: form a sea or lake, of a river; of islands, lie out in the open sea, Id.10.2.19

πέλαγος.definition: gen. pl. Hdt.4.85; of parts of the sea , freq. with geographical epith., A.Ag.659, etc., cf. Hdt.4.85 ; S.Aj.702 , cf. Luc.Icar.3; Th.4.24

πελαγόω.definition: turn into sea, flood, Ach. Tat.4.12

πελάζω.definition: less freq. c. gen., Hp.Mul.1.34; . . . . light may come near the ships, S.Aj.709 ; Id.Ph.1407 ; Call.Ap.88 ; Th.2.77, Plb.21.6.3; also E.Med.101

πελεκάω.definition: hew or shape with an axe, Od.5.244; sens. obsc. , Arar.5

πελεμίζω.definition: Ep. inf. Il.16.766: Ep. aor; shake or drive from his post, Il.16.108: aor. Pass. , 4.535; Pi.N.8.29

πελματίζω.definition: scrape the sole of the foot, Et.Havn. ap; sole boots, PMasp.5.18

πέλω.definition: and only pres., impf., and aor.:—Act; become, Od.1.393, cf. Il.24.219; 13.103: Theoc.14.68: . . quite otherwise does my spear become sharp, i. e. in a very different way does my spear prove its edge, Il.11.392, cf. A.…

πεμπάζω.definition: prop. count on the five fingers, i.e; metaph., count up, reckon over, A.R.4.1748:—Med., ib.350.—In Prose is more common

πεμπαστής.definition: Dor. one who counts: as a Verbal c. acc., reviewing by tens of thousands, A.Pers.980

πέμπω.definition: Ep. inf. Od.13.48, 10.18: Ion; folld. by Advbs., Od.19.281, 24.418; Il.16.445; Od.9.461; Il.18.452, etc.; . . was conducting or convoying Patroclus to Hades, 23.137

πένομαι.definition: used only in pres. and impf; intr., toil, work, . ., Od.10.348: were busy preparing a meal, 4.624; Il.24.124

πενόομαι.definition: = aor. part. poor, needy, v.l. for in Men.Mon.43

πεντάβραχυς.definition: foot consisting of five short syllables, Choerob.in Heph.p.247C

πεντάμορφος.definition: having five shapes, of evil, Simp.in Epict.pp.71,72 D

πεντώνυμος.definition: called by five names, Tz.Proll.Com.p.29 K

πέπανσις.definition: ripening, of fruits; Medic., maturation, of tumours and the like , Arist.Mete.380a21

πέπνυμαι.definition: Ep. pf. Pass. with pres. sense, to be; more freq. to be wise, . . Il.24.377: 23.440: imper. Thgn.29: plpf. with impf. sense, Od.23.210: most freq. in part. of persons, Il.3.203, Od.3.52; also of things, 1.361, Il.7.27…

περαιόω.definition: carry over or across; intr. in Act., Id.2.67

πέρασις.definition: crossing, a completing of; Pythag. name for nine, Theol.Ar.57

περάω.definition: late Ep. part. IG12.441.3; more freq. pass right across or through a space, traverse, freq. of water, Od.6.272, 24.118; 5.174; Hes.Op.738: Alc.l. c.; Pi.N.3.21: Hdt.4.115: A.Pr.792, 718; S.Aj.461; also pass a barrier …

πέρθω.definition: Il.18.342: fut. 21.584: aor. 1; get by plunder, take at the sack of a town, Il.1.125: . . E.El.316

περιάγνυμι.definition: and : pf. part. (in; once in Hom., of sound, the voice is broken all round, i. e. spreads all round, Il.16.78; echo broke forth around them, Hes.Sc.279

περιᾴδω.definition: go about singing, Luc.Salt.27; Pass., to be buzzed about, Plu.2.663d

περιαθρέω.definition: inspect all round, consider narrowly; look round upon, Hld.10.35

περιανθέω.definition: bloom: hence, glow all round, of heat, Plu.2.648a

περιβαίνω.definition: bestride, as a rider does a horse, Plu.Pyrrh.11, 2.213e; Malch.p.394 D.; those mounted on the elephants, D.S.17.88; of the male camel, Arist.HA540a14; Ar.Lys.979

περιβάλλω.definition: metaph., put round or upon a person, i. e. invest him with it, , Hdt.1.129, E.Ion829; Id.HF304; Id.Ph.189 ; Id.IA934; i.e. make him faint- hearted, Id.Or.1031; impute blame to . . , Pall.in Hp.12.283 C.:—Pass., c. acc…

περιβιόω.definition: survive, aor. inf. Plu.Cor.11: fut; trans., in fut., keep alive, v.l. in ib.Ex.22.18 cod. A

περιβλύζω.definition: and boil or bubble all round; c.acc., cause to gush around, Philostr.VA3.25

περιβύω.definition: stop up round about, in Pass; stuff in all round, Luc.Gall.11

περιγίγνομαι.definition: Ion. and later fut. Th.4.27, etc.: aor. Hdt.1.122, etc.: pf. ib.82, etc.; Th.1.69, etc.:-to be superior to others, prevail over, overcome: Constr. in full, c. gen. pers. et dat. rei, 11.23.318; Od.8.102, cf. 252; cf. …

περιγνάμπτω.definition: double a headland, Od.9.80; intr., curve, Arat.790

περιδαίω.definition: in Pass. to be exceedingly heated, Opp.H.5.411: metaph., I burn with love for him, A.R.4.58

περιδέρω.definition: dissect off all round, Gal.2.691:—Pass., to be flayed, Antyll. ap. Orib.50.2.4

περιδίω.definition: = to be in great fear for, c. dat., used by Hom. only in 3sg. impf. and always in tmesi, Il.9.433, 11.557: folld. by relat. clause, 5.566: without dat., . . 17.666, cf. Od.22.96

περιδρύπτω.definition: tear all round, peel the bark off a tree, AP9.706 :—Pass., had the skin all torn from off his arms, Il.23.395, cf. Q.S.4.540; Ph.1.311; Id.2.527; Ach. Tat.1.12

περιδύω.definition: strip off, Il.11.100; c.acc.pers., strip, Antipho2.2.5; App.BC5.68, etc.: metaph., deprive of authority, J.AJ13.15.3

περίειμι.definition: to be superior to another, surpass, excel, c.gen.pers., 11.8.27, cf. Emp.113, Hdt.3.146, X.Mem.3.7.7: c. acc. rei, Il.13.631; Od.18.248, cf. 19.326, etc.; Il.1.258, cf. Od.1.66: later c. dat. rei, Pl.Prt.342b, cf. Smp…

περιέλκω.definition: Att. aor. later; metaph., drag one's good name in the mire, Jul.Or.7.214d

περιεργία.definition: futility, needless questioning; over-elaboration, Men.Rh.p.342 S.; curiosities of cakes, Luc.Nigr.33

περιέχω.definition: also Th.5.71; Aeol. Sapph.Supp.25.9, Theoc.30.3: fut. : aor. inf. aor. Med. inf. embrace, surround, Lys.7.28; Pl.Ti.25a, cf. Arist.Mete.354a6; Pl.Men.85a, cf.Arist.Mech.851a14; Id.Mete.375a31; IG42.122.21 ; the envelo…

περιηγής.definition: lying in a circle, of the Cyclades lying; of the arms, tied behind one, APl.4.195

περιηχέω.definition: Pass., to be noised abroad, to be celebrated, Ph.Bybl. ap. Eus.PE1.10: c. inf., Cod.Just.10.11.8 Intr

περιηχή.definition: noise all around, Choerob. Rh.p.249 S

περιθάλπω.definition: warm all round, cherish, Gal.14.304:—Pass., Aen.Gaz.Thphr.p.70 B

περιίστημι.definition: bring round, Arist.Pol.1304a33; Pl.Ax. l.c.; . . Heraclid.Pont. ap. Ath.12.537c; esp. into a worse state, . . Isoc.6.47, cf. Aeschin.3.82; Plb.3.8.2; Hdn.7.3.5; convert, Epicur.Ep.2p.51 U.; transfer, D.40.20; D.H.3.3

περίκειμαι.definition: inf. fut. -used as Pass. of lie round about, c. dat., lying with his arms round him, Il.19.4; there was a case round the bow, Od.21.54; . . Alc.15; Pi.O.8.76; Hdn.6.1.1; Plu.Dio56: c. acc., Luc.Astr.3: with a Prep., A…

περικήδομαι.definition: to be very anxious or concerned about, c. gen., Od.3.219; Pi.N.10.54; take care of his substance for him, Od.14.527

περικλάω.definition: twist round, bend, Thphr.Ign.53; in Optics, refract, Cleom.2.1

περίκλινον.definition: couch all round a table, f.l. for; couch-cover, Gloss

περίκομμα.definition: that which is cut off all round; = II, Plu.2.765c

περικωνέω.definition: smear all over with pitch, black shoes, Ar.V.600

περιμένω.definition: wait for, await, c. acc. pers., Hdt.4.89; require, expect, Id.2.172e

περιμηχανάομαι.definition: prepare very craftily, contrive cunningly, . . Od.7.200; 14.340

περιναιετάω.definition: dwell round about or in the; of cities, to be or lie near, Od.4.177

περιξέω.definition: polish all round, Theoc.22.50; scrape all round, Hp.Mul.2.144

περιοδεία.definition: or going round, circuit; patrolling, rounds, Aen.Tact.1.1 , al

περιπέλομαι.definition: Hom. only in Ep. aor. 2 part; move round, be round about, only in part

περιπέμπω.definition: send round from one place to another; send round to a number of places, Hdt.1.48

περιπίτνω.definition: poet. for c. acc., comes over or upon the heart, A.Th.834

περιπλέκω.definition: aor. 2 part. Pass; twine round with something, Thphr.CP5.15.6

περιπλέω.definition: Ion. sail or swim round, abs; metaph., to be unstable, slip about, Hp.Fract.4

περίπνοος.definition: contr. blown round about, airy, Thphr.HP5.1.11

περιπροχέομαι.definition: to be poured all round, used by Hom. in aor. part., . . love rushing in a flood over my heart overcame it, Il.14.316

περιρρέω.definition: fut. Arist.Cael.287b10: aor. 1 inf; c. acc., flow round, Od.9.388; Hdt.2.29, cf. 127; Pl.Phd.111a; . . Lycurg.l.c. codd.; of persons, Pl.Chrm.155d:—Pass., to be surrounded by water, X.An.1.5.4, Arist.Mu.393a11, al

περισαίνω.definition: Ep. wag the tail round, fawn upon, Od.16.4; 10.215; of Opp.H.4.361: metaph., Orph.L.430, cf. Them.Or.7.92d, 21.258d; Simp.in Epict.p.52 D

περισείομαι.definition: Pass., to be shaken all round, the hair floated round, Il.19.382, 22.315

περισθενέω.definition: to be exceeding strong, part. Od.22.368

περισοβέω.definition: chase about, push round the; run bustling round, Ar.Av.1425

περιστείχω.definition: go round about, c. acc., Od.4.277, cf. AP5.138 : abs., Call.Aet.1.1.13, dub. in Alc.Com.35

περιστέλλω.definition: fut. S.Aj.1170:—dress, clothe, wrap; Rhet., employ compression, Corn.Rh.p.396 H

περιστεναχίζομαι.definition: Med., = foreg., resound all round or re-echo with . . , Od.23.146, cf. 10.454 ; ib.10:— later in Act., Q.S.12.415

περιστένω.definition: Ep. make narrow, compress, contract, of wolves, Il.16.163; Q.S.3.23, cf. 14.607, Opp.H.4.458

περιστέφω.definition: enwreathe, surround, Od.5.303; Plu.Arist.9; Id.2.245e; of the serpent Pytho, Call.Del.93:—Pass., Orph.Fr.186: metaph., Aphth.Prog.3

περιστρέφω.definition: whirl round, of one preparing to throw; tie his hands behind him, Lys.1.27:—Pass., to be twisted, of an intestine, Gal.8.388

περιστροφίς.definition: wooden implement that is turned; handle for turning a fuller's press, ib.135

περισύρω.definition: metaph., satirize, ridicule, Eust.1816.46; tear off, pick off, LXXGe.30.37

περιτέλλομαι.definition: Pass., go or come round, mostly of Time; of the sun and stars, rise above the horizon, Alc.39, Arat.215, 232

περιτέμνω.definition: Ep. and Ion. cut or clip round; of circumcision, Hdt.2.104, cf. D.C.79.11; D.S.1.28, cf. LXXJo.5.2, al., PCair.Zen.76.13 , etc.:— Med., Hdt.2.36,104, cf. D.S.3.32; LXXGe.34.24: abs., practise circumcision, Hdt.2.104:—…

περίτηγμα.definition: that which is cast off in smelting, dross, scum: metaph., Chrysipp.Stoic.3.85

περιτήκω.definition: melt, melt away, Hp.Vict.1.13; cover with a coat of tin, Pl.Criti.116b

περιτίθημι.definition: place or put round, put on; metaph., bestow, confer upon, Hdt.1.129, 3.81, 142, Simon.100; Th.4.87, Isoc.5.149, etc.; put reproach, dishonour upon him, Antipho5.18, Th.6.89; Aeschin.2.103; Antipho2.3.1; put the Median…

περιτίλλω.definition: pluck all round, strip, strip the

περιτρέχω.definition: run about everywhere, Cratin.52; Alex.174.1; Pl.Smp.173a, cf. Lys.30.21: generally, to be in motion, circulate, Plot.6.3.24; flexibility of movement, of a surgeon operating, Plu.2.67e. 3. metaph., to be current, in vo…

περιτρέω.definition: flee round about, the people fled on all sides, Il.11.676

περιτρίβω.definition: rub or wear away all round; smear, Nonn.D.6.190, 41.110

περιτρομέω.definition: tremble, Q.S.13.184,al.: c. acc., tremble at, Id.3.182,364: c. gen., tremble by reason of, Arat.861, Opp.H.4.194: c. dat., tremble for, ib.1.293,4.202:—Med., all the flesh crept on his limbs, Od.18.77: abs., Q.S.1.477

περιτροπέω.definition: Ion. and Ep. form of; intr., a revolving year, Il.2.295

περιφαίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be visible all round; shine around, Plu.2.932b

περιφιμόω.definition: close all round, Afric.Cest.p.45 V., Ps.Democr.Alch.p.48B., cf. Zos.Alch.p.141 B

περιφράζομαι.definition: Med. with aor. 1 Pass; Act., express periphrastically, D.H.Amm.2.4: abs., use periphrasis, Phld.Po.5.28:— Pass., D.H.Th.29; . . , Plu.2.407a

περιχέω.definition: Ep. aor. , pour; of persons, Hld.9.1:— freq. in Pass., crowding round, Hdt.9.120; Pl.R.488c, cf. Plt.268c, X.HG2.2.21

περιχρίω.definition: smear or cover over; pour as unguent over, J.AJ7.14.5, cf. Nonn.D.14.175

περίχυμα.definition: that which is poured round or; that which is diffused around the earth, atmosphere, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44

περιχώομαι.definition: Med., to be exceeding angry, Il.9.449; 14.266

περιψαύω.definition: touch, attack a part, of pains, Nic.Al.122

περιωπή.definition: place commanding a wide view; circumspection, to show much caution in a thing, Th.4.87

περκάζω.definition: become dark, turn dark, of; metaph., of young men, whose beard begins to darken their faces, Call.Lav.Pall.76

πέρνημι.definition: simply, sell , Is. l.c.:—Pass., to be sold, esp. for exportation, Sol. l. c., Hdt.1.156, A.Ch.915, E.Ion310; Hdt.2.54, 56; SIG45.38 ; interpol. in Pl.Phd.69b; Id.Lg.850a; the tax of 2 per cent. having been sold or let…

περονάω.definition: pierce, transfix; Med., buckle on one's mantle, one's robe, Il.10.133, 14.180; Theoc.14.66, cf. A.R.1.722

περόνη.definition: pin or tongue of a buckle or; pin for twisting ropes round, on board ship, A.R.1.567

περόνιον.definition: Dim. of small peg or pin; shackle or ring into which a bolt fits, Ph.Bel.76.4

πεσσεία.definition: Att. game resembling draughts or; in Music, repetition of same note, Cleonid.Harm.14

πεσσεύω.definition: Att. play at draughts, Heraclit.52, Pl.Alc.1.110e, R.487b, X.Mem.3.9.9, etc.: prov., fortune gambles with human affairs, Ph.2.85

πέσσω.definition: Il.4.513 (no other tense in Hom. exc. in the; of the West wind, ripen fruit, Od.7.119: generally, bring to maturity, Arist.GA780b10; also Id.Pr.944a13

πετάννυμι.definition: and ; later Luc.Cal.21; poet. : fut. E.IT1135 ; Att. Men.26,458: aor. Ar.Pl.731, etc.; Ep. Hom. : pf. D.S.17.115:—Med., Ep. aor. Nonn.D.2.704:—Pass., aor. Ep. Od.21.50, E.Cyc.497 : pf. Hom. , Orac. ap. Hdt.1.62, Plb.3…

πέτασμα.definition: anything spread out, of the feelers of the polypus, Arist.HA541b6: pl., carpets, . . A.Ag.909

πέτομαι.definition: metaph. and proverbial usages:—to be on the wing, flutter, of uncertain hopes, Pi.P.8.90; S.OT487 ; of fickle natures, E.Ba.332; Ar.Ec.899; a bird ever on the wing, Id.Av.169; 'you are chasing a butterfly', Pl.Euthphr…

πετρόω.definition: turn into stone, petrify, mostly in Pass; Pass., to be frozen, ib.47.591

πεύθομαι.definition: older form of Od.3.87,al. only twice), Hes.Th.463, Mimn.14.2, Pi.P.4.38, 109, A.Ch.679, S.OT604, E.IA1138, Herod.6.38: impf. Il.17.408, E.Rh.767:—Act. give notice, lay an information, Leg.Gort.8.55, SIG525.9

πεύκη.definition: pine, esp. Pinus Laricio, Corsican pine; anything made from the wood of the torch of pine-wood, A.Ag.288 , S.OT214 , E.Ion716 , etc.; A.Fr.171

πεφύκω.definition: Ep. pres. formed from pf. = hence impf. Hes.Op.149, Th.152

πηγάζω.definition: spring, gush forth; c. acc. cogn., gush forth with, AP9.404 ; Heraclit.All.9; Procl.in Cra.p.52 P

πήγνυμι.definition: Hdt.4.72 , Thphr.HP6.6.9; stick or fix in, Il.4.460, etc. ; 13.570; Od.23.276 ; 11.77 ; Hes.Op.430; Pi.N.7.26; fix in the earth, plant, S.El.420, cf. Aj.821; pitch a tent, And.4.30, Pl.Lg.817c ; Th.6.66; X.Cyn.6.7; pl…

πηδάλιον.definition: steering-paddle, rudder; in pl., of the oars by which the nautilus is said to steer himself, Arist.HA622b13; of the long hind legs of the locust and grasshopper, ib.532a29,535b12, cf. IA710a3

πηδάω.definition: E.Ion717 , etc.; Dor. 3sg. Sophr.20; Lacon. imper. Ar.Lys.1317 ; Ion. part. Herod.3.96, 4.61: fut. Thphr.Char.21.6, Pl.Ly.216a, Alex.124.16; later APl.4.54*, 142: aor. Il.14.455, etc.: pf. Aesop.203, Hp.Art.47, X.HG7.…

πήδημα.definition: leap, bound, A.Pers.95,305; beating or throbbing of the heart, E.Ba.1288; Plu.2.83b

πηλίκος.definition: interrog. correl. to; of what age, Xenoph.22.5

πηλόγονος.definition: born from clay, = used of the giants in Call.Jov.3

πημαίνω.definition: Il.15.42: fut. S.Aj.1314, OC837; Ion. Il.24.781: aor. 3.299, S.Tr.715, Pl.R.364c; Dor. part. IG12.1085.8:—Med., fut. Ar.Ach.842 , also in pass. sense, S.Aj.1155: Ep. aor. Q.S.13.379:—Pass., aor. :—plunge into ruin, un…

πηνῖτις.definition: the weaver, i. e. Athena, Ael.NA6.57; Dor. dat. cj. Mein. for in AP6.289

πήρωμα.definition: mutilated or imperfect animal; = Id.GA746b32, Gal.UP14.6

πηχίζω.definition: measure by the cubit, Sm., Al.Ez.43.13, Supp.Epigr.6.636

πιδύω.definition: gush forth, AP9.322 , 10.13 ; Plu.Aem.14, cf. Antig.Mir.144: —Med., Nic.Th.302. exc. in Nic. l.c.]

πιέζω.definition: impf. Ep. Od.12.174, etc.: fut; press or weigh down, of a heavy weight, Pi.P.1.19, cf. Ar.Pax1032:—and in Pass., . . Id.Ra.30, cf. X.Cyr.7.5.11: metaph., oppress, distress, Hdt.5.35; A.Ch.250; ib.301; E.Alc.894 ; Ar.N…

πίεσμα.definition: Dor. and later Gr. anything; pulpy mass left after pressing, pomace, Gal.10.911, Gp.20.28: pl., of cakes of olive-pulp, PSI9.1030.11

πιεστέος.definition: to be pressed, Hp.Fract.25; one must squeeze, press, Orib.Fr.48

πιθήκιον.definition: Dim. of Lat. pithecium; weight hung between two ships coupled for carrying engines of war, Ath.Mech.32.11

πίλημα.definition: compressed wool or hair, felt; anything made thereof, hat , Call.Fr.124, 125

πιλνάω.definition: = bring near, once in Hes., . . . . brings them to earth, Op.510; also intr., thou drawest nigh to the house, h.Cer.115 :—elsewh. Pass. , draw near to, approach, c. dat., the chariots went close to the ground, Il.23.3…

πιλοφορέω.definition: wear a or apex, like the Roman flamines, App.BC1.65

πιλόω.definition: = of the effect of cold, contract, opp. Thphr.CP3.23.5:—Pass., ib.1.12.3; Democr. ap. Placit.4.1.4

πίμπλημι.definition: in pres. and impf. formed like Aeol; fill full, satisfy, glut, E.Cyc.146, etc

πίμπρημι.definition: pres. and impf. non-thematic; imper; = I.1, blow up, distend, in Pass., Hp.Nat.Mul.10, Flat.8, Nic.Al.477, Act.Ap.28.6 ; IG42.122.123 :—Act., Arist.HA522b28, Dsc.4.32

πινύσκω.definition: and Ep. aor. aor. Pass. make prudent, admonish, correct, Il.14.249; Naumach. ap. Stob.4.23.7; . . A.Pers.830; Call.Dian.152; makes the days calm, Simon.12; simply, teach, Orph.Fr.178:—Pass., Pythag ap. Iamb.VP28.146

πίνω.definition: Ep. inf. and Il.4.346; abs., drink, Od.2.305; 5.94, 6.249, cf. Il.24.476, etc.; going to drink after pasture, 13.493; Alc.20; Simon.14; Pl.Smp.176e; Id.Lg.775b; Cratin.124; X.Cyr.8.3.41; ib.1.3.9; Philem.9: in pf. to …

πιππίζω.definition: pipe, cheep, or chirp like young birds, Ar.Av.306

πίπτω.definition: Aeol. acc. to Gramm. in Hilgard Exc. ex libris Herodiani p.28 ; poet. subj. Pl.Com.153.5: Ep. impf. Il.8.67, etc. ; Ion. Emp.59.2: fut. A.Ch.971 , etc.; Ion.3pl. Il.11.824, 3sg. Hdt.7.163, 168: aor. inf. Il.13.178, et…

πίσσανθος.definition: the oily fluid that rises to the surface when the raw pitch is left to stand, Gal.11.520

πιστεύω.definition: fut. plpf. Act.Ap.14.23; comply, S.OT625, cf. 646; opp. Id.Tr.1228

πιστόω.definition: make trustworthy, bind him; Pass., to be made trustworthy, give a pledge or warrant, h.Merc.536; E.IA66; . . bind yourselves to me by oath . . , Od.15.436

πίστωμα.definition: assurance, warrant, pledge, mostly; confirmation of an argument, in pl., Phld.Rh.1.285 S., Sign.19

πίτνημι.definition: poet. form of spread out, Il.21.7; stretching out his arms to me, Od.11.392; Pi.N.5.11; AP10.6 : metaph., excite, flutter, S.Ichn.359:—Pass., . . Il.22.402; E.El.713 ; . . AP7.711 :—also only Hes.Sc.291

πιτυρίς.definition: small kind of olive, of the colour of bran, which was gathered before it was ripe, and then preserved, acc. Call.Fr.50, cf. Philem.Gloss. ap. Ath.2.56c. prop., but in Call.l.c.]

πιφαύσκω.definition: redupl. form of , only; declare, utter, . . Od.11.442; 22.131; Emp.17.15

πλαδάω.definition: to be flaccid, of the flesh; have a 'splashy' stomach, Dsc.Eup.2.9, cf.Gal.13.145

πλαδδιάω.definition: talk nonsense, Lacon. word in Ar.Lys., inf. 171, imper. 990

πλάζω.definition: Ep.impf. Od.2.396: aor; baffle, thwart, balk, esp. mentally, . . Il.2.132; balked or bewildered them as they drank, Od.2.396; i.e. became drunk, Pi.Fr.166; E.HF1189 ; Hp.Ep.18; embarrass, trip up, AP7.365 ; wavered ai…

πλακόω.definition: face with marble slabs, BCH21.48 :—Pass., Gloss

πλανάω.definition: fut. LXX4 Ki.4.28, etc. :—Pass. and; lead from the subject, in talking, D.19.335

πλάνησις.definition: making to wander : dispersing; metaph., misleading, S.E.M.7.394

πλάστης.definition: moulder, modeller, in clay or wax; creator, Ph.1.434

πλατειάζω.definition: Dor. slap with the flat hand; pronounce broadly, like the Dorians, Theoc.15.88

πλατυσμός.definition: widening, enlarging, dilatation; metaph., boasting, bragging, Timo20

πλεθρίζω.definition: run the metaph., 'draw the long bow', Thphr.Char.23.2

πλειονάζω.definition: have more than one meaning or application; to be in excess, IG5.1390.39

πλεκτάνη.definition: anything twined or wreathed; Medic., mastoid growth in the uterus, Diocl.Fr.27, Eudem. and Praxag. ap. Gal.2.890

πλεκτή.definition: coil, wreath, . . A.Ch.248; twisted rope, cord, string, E.Tr.958, 1010, Pl.Com.21

πλέκω.definition: Pi.O.6.86, etc.: fut. AP5.146 : aor. Il.14.176, etc.: pf. , Hp.Oss.16, ibid., but ib.17:-Med., fut. Perict. ap. Stob.4.28.19: aor. Od.10.168, Ar.Lys.790:-Pass., fut. A.Pr.1079 ; Gal.6.873: aor. A.Eu.259 , Pl.Plt.283a,…

πλεομελής.definition: with more than the normal number of limbs, coined word in Iamb.in Nic.p.32 P

πλευμάω.definition: or have disease of the lungs, Hp.Morb.2.48

πλεύρωμα.definition: only pl., sides, of a man; cross-rail, Ath. Mech.17.13

πλέω.definition: to be conveyed by sea, Th.3.114; metaph., while [the ship of] our country bearing us is on an even keel, S.Ant.190; D.19.250; Pl.Lg.813d; E.Fr.397; also Ar.Pax699. -, cf. Skt. plávate 'float', 'swim', Lat. pluit; with…

πληθόχορος.definition: much-dancing, or, gathering a large troupe of dancers, Id

πλήθω.definition: poet. pf. Pherecr.29; trans. only in later Poets, AP14.7, Opp.C.1.126, Q.S.6.345:—Pass., A.R.3.1392, 4.564, AP5.232 , Q.S.14.607; BCH50.44

πλήρωμα.definition: that which fills, complement; satiety of the feast, E.Med.203 ; their fill of cheese, Id.Cyc.209

πληρωτής.definition: one who completes; one who fills up documents, Lyd.Mag.3.11, 68

πλήσσω.definition: Nic.Al.456, present used by Hom. and Att; sting, Sammelb.1267.6

πλινθήϊον.definition: poet. for of part of the zodiac, Doroth. ap. Heph.Astr.3.7

πλινθίς.definition: Dim. of stone cut in the; square or check, Callix.1

πλίσσομαι.definition: aor. 1 Ar.Ach.218: pf. Archil.58:—cross the legs, as in trotting, well they galloped, well they trotted, Od.6.318:—Act., cj. in Call.Dian.243; cf. Hsch

πλύνω.definition: Ep. impf. Il.22.155: fut. Ar.Th.248, D.39.11; Ion. and Ep. Od.6.31,59: aor. Ep. Od.6.93, Ar.Pl.1062, D.54.9:-Med., fut. LXXNu.31.24 : aor. part. LXXLe.13.6, Hdt.4.73:-Pass., fut. Com.Adesp.715: aor. 3sg. subj. Thphr.H…

πλωάς.definition: = sailing or floating about, A.R.2.1053 :—also Thphr. ap. Plu.2.292c; floating islands in Lake Copais, Thphr.HP4.10.2, 4.12.4

πλωτήρ.definition: sailor, seaman, Archyt. ap; swimmer, Nonn.D.1.65, al., Musae.2; of fishes, Opp.H.2.196

πνευματόω.definition: turn into vapour; Pass., to be filled with wind, Epicur.Ep.2pp.44,47 U

πνέω.definition: poet. as always in Hom. exc. Od.5.469: fut; breathe, send forth an odour, . . Od.4.446; Poll.2.75, etc.: abs., Dsc.3.80

πνῖγμα.definition: choking, . . Hp.Epid.7.26; to have it fast by the throat, Cephisodot. ap.Arist.Rh.1411a7

πνιγμός.definition: choking, suffocation, Hp.Coac.61; stifling heat, Men.Rh.p.351S

ποάζω.definition: weed, cj. in Philem.116.4; of ground, produce grass, Str.5.3.8, 12.2.7; of the sea, appear grassy with seaweed, Id.16.4.7

ποδαρκής.definition: succouring with the feet; a day of swift feet, i.e. on which swift runners contended, Pi.O.13.38; the sacred field of swift courses, i.e. the Pythian race-course, Id.P.5.33

ποδίζω.definition: bind or tie the feet:—Pass., to have the feet; furnish with feet, Theol.Ar.55

ποδισμός.definition: measuring by feet, = Lat. pedatura; in Metric, scansion, Eust.456.39: hence, metaph., of the pulse, Ruf.Syn.Puls.4.4

ποδόμακτρον.definition: towel for wiping the feet, Gloss

ποδοψόφος.definition: making a noise with the foot or feet, ib

ποδόω.definition: tighten a sail with the sheet, Eust.1534.26; Pass., to be furnished with feet, Nicostr. ap. Simp.in Cat.369.10

ποθέω.definition: Od.1.343, etc.; Aeol. Sapph.23; Ep. inf; of things, crave, require, E.Fr.467; Pl.Smp.204d, cf. Prt.352a

ποθή.definition: = c. gen., longing, desire for; c. gen. rei, want of . . , Od.15.514,546

ποθίζω.definition: = stick tightly, of a plaster, Aret.CA2.3

ποθίκω.definition: Dor. and Boeot. for belong, c. dat., IG9.189.10 , 7.3083 , etc

ποιέω.definition: Dor. IG4.800 , etc.: Ep. impf; create, bring into existence, Hes.Op.110, cf. Th.161, 579, etc.; the creator, Pl.Ti.76c; D.4.11:—Med., beget, And.1.124; Id.4.22; = X.Cyr.5.3.19, D.57.43; conceive, Pl.Smp.203b:—Act. in …

ποικιλία.definition: marking with various colours; in pl., pieces of embroidery, X.Mem.3.8.10

ποικιλίς.definition: an unknown bird which eats the lark's eggs, Arist.HA609a6

ποικίλλω.definition: fut. Choerob.in An.Ox.2.250: aor. 1; embroider garments, etc., Inscr.Délos l.c.; Pi.N.8.15: metaph., diversify, vary, E.Cyc.339, cf. Pl.Lg.927e, Plu.Mar.23; vary the order of march with troops of horse, X.Eq.Mag.4.3; …

ποιμαίνω.definition: every country has been traversed , A.Eu.249; guide, govern, E.Fr.744; Luc.Am.6

ποινή.definition: blood-money, were-gild, fine paid by the slayer to the kinsmen of the slain, c. gen. pers., Il.14.483; 13.659, cf. 9.633; 18.498. 2. generally, price paid, satisfaction, requital, penalty, Od.23.312; Il.21.28; 16.398;…

ποινήλατος.definition: pursued by the furies, Anon; inflicted by them, Simp.in Epict.p.117 D

ποίνιμος.definition: avenging, punishing; in good sense, bringing return or recompense, cj. in Pi.P.2.17

ποιονόμος.definition: feeding on grass or herbs; proparox. with rich grassy fields, Id.Supp.50

ποιπνύω.definition: impf. Ep. Il.24.475: aor; later c. acc., Emp.73; . . Pythag. ap. Porph.VP40 codd.; Orac. ap. Phleg.37 J

ποκάς.definition: wool, hair, Ar.Th.567 , dub. in PThead.8.9

ποκίζω.definition: = shear wool:—Med., shear for oneself, Theoc.5.26

πολέμαρχος.definition: chieftain, war-lord; the title of high officers in several Greek states

πολεμίζω.definition: Il.1.168,al.; Ep. inf. 9.337:-also , 8.428, al.: fut. or 24.667, 2.328:-poet. form of wage war, fight, with one, Il.9.337, al.; 8.428, 20.85; jointly with . . , 9.352; 2.121; Pi.O.9.32 ; Ar.Nu.419:-Med., Pi.N.8.29 . I…

πολεύω.definition: intr., turn or go about, go about the city, i.e. live therein, Od.22.223; in Astrol., the planet presiding over a day, SerapioinCat.Cod.Astr.1.99, PMag.Leid.W.5.47, Paul.Al.I.3; PMag.Par.1.545, cf. Iamb.Myst.3.30

πολίζω.definition: build a city or cities on or in a place, X.An.6.6.4; Str.8.5.4; Plu.Rom.9:—Pass., Hdt.5.13.—Ep., Ion., X., and later Prose

πολιορκία.definition: Ion. siege of a city; metaph., besieging, pestering, v.l. in Plu.Sull.25

πολίτης.definition: fellow-citizen , Sapph.Supp.1.14, etc.; A.Th.1; And.1.139; Lys.20.12; Pl.Prt.339e: and by a Com. metaph., Amphis36

πολυάνωρ.definition: with many men, much-; wife of many husbands, A.Ag.62

πολύγονον.definition: knot-grass, Polygonum; mare's tail, Hippuris vulgaris, Dsc.4.5

πολύζωος.definition: = long-lived, of a very aged man, Com.Adesp.892; Opp.C.3.117

πολύζῳος.definition: consisting of many animals; multiplex animal, Plot.2.3.7

πολύθεος.definition: of or belonging to many gods; believing in many gods, Procop.Arc.11; polytheism, Ph.1.41, al

πολύθρεπτος.definition: much-nourished, the many flowers that grow, ib.43.6

πολύθριξ.definition: with much hair, of persons; Subst., = Plin.HN25.132

πολύθυρος.definition: with many doors or windows; with many plates or leaves, . . E.IT727

πολυκέρως.definition: many-horned, the slaughter of many horned cattle, S.Aj.55

πολύκυκος.definition: much troubled, of the sea, Porph.adIl.2.145

πολύλοπος.definition: with many layers of bark or wood, Thphr.HP1.5.2, 5.1.6

πολύοζος.definition: with many branches, Diog.Apoll.6; of trees, Thphr.HP3.13.3,7.2.8: Comp., ib.1.8.5

πολύπλοος.definition: contr. of or for many voyages, Men.Rh.p.352 S

πολύπορος.definition: furnishing abundant harvests; with many passages, Plu.2.650c

πολύσιος.definition: with many defects or blemishes, Vett.Val.111.12

πολύτιτος.definition: worthy of high honour, Orac. ap

πολυφορέω.definition: to be prolific, bear or yield much; Pass., to be found in a variety of forms, Eust.1502.58

πολύφρων.definition: gen. ingenious, inventive; embodying much thought, Orac. ap. Dam.Pr.161

πολύχειρ.definition: with many hands, many-handed; with a large band of soldiers, A.Pers.83 ; Heraclit.All.25

πολυχοΐα.definition: diversity, variety, Thphr.HP1.14.5:—also abundant crop, Max.486

πολύχοος.definition: capable of great diffusion, Hp.Vict.2.56; in large quantity, Heraclit.All.33

πολυωπής.definition: with many holes or meshes, AP6.27 ; Nic.Al.323; i.e. honeycombs, ib.450:—late poet. fem

πομπεία.definition: leading in procession, solemn procession; abuse, ribaldry, such as was allowed to those who took part in the processions at the festivals of Dionysus and Demeter, D.18.11, Men.Per.Fr.4 : metaph., the mock that fate ma…

πομπεῖον.definition: vessel employed in solemn; at Athens, storehouse where such vessels were kept, D.34.39, D.L.2.43,6.22

πομπεύς.definition: gen. Ion. Att.pl; one who takes part in a procession, Th.6.58, IG22.334.14

πομπεύω.definition: poet. Iterat. Theoc.2.68; carry sinning Vestal Virgins in procession, D.H.8.89

πομπή.definition: conduct, escort; concrete, an escort, Id.Eu.1034

πομπός.definition: conductor, escort, guide; c. gen. rei, conveyor, carrier of these suppliant offerings, A.Ch.86; ib.147

πονέω.definition: abs., work hard, Il.2.409; he ought to suffer toil in praying, 10.117; . . , with which he did his work, of Hephaestus, 18.413, cf. Od.16.13; . . were busied about their supper, Il.24.444, cf. Hdt.2.63, Pl.Phlb.58e; s…

πόντισμα.definition: that which is cast into the sea, esp. as an offering, E.Hel.1548

ποντιστής.definition: one who casts into the sea, Paus.8.52.2

ποντοκύκη.definition: woman who disturbs the sea, i.e. shrew, prob. in Com.Adesp.893

ποντοπορεύω.definition: pass over the sea, Ep.inf. Od.5.277: elsewh. in part., . . ib.278, cf.7.267: later in med., Orac. ap. Plu.Thes.24

ποντοπορέω.definition: = foreg., sea-sailing, Od.11.11, cf. LXXPr.24.54, Q.S.7.397; sail the open sea. opp. a coasting voyage, Plu.Dio25; . . AP10.74

ποντόω.definition: throw into the sea, Nic.Dam.10 J; Pass., become a sea, Q.S.14.604

πορθέω.definition: collat. form of; in pres. and impf., sts. endeavour to destroy, besiege a town, Hdt.1.162, Decr. ap. D.18.164, D.S.12.34, 15.4

πορθμός.definition: ferry or place crossed by a; generally, the sea, Pi.I.4.57

πόρισμα.definition: Geom., deduction from a previous; a kind of proposition intermediate between a theorem and a problem, defined by Papp.648.18 sqq., Procl.in Euc.p.301F

ποριστής.definition: one who supplies or provides; the name used by robbers of themselves, Arist.Rh.1405a26

πόρπαξ.definition: handle of a shield; part of the headgear of a horse, E.Rh.385

πορπάω.definition: aor. imper. A.Pr.61:—fasten with a brooch, pin down, l.c

πορσύνω.definition: fut. A.Supp.522, Ep; generally, prepare, provide, Pi.I.6.8; ib.4.61; S.OC341; Id.Fr.593.5; E.Med.1020; Id.El.625; Id.Supp.132; X.Cyr.4.2.47:—Med., provide for oneself, A.Pers.375

πορφύρεος.definition: of blood, gushing, Il.17.361; so, onrushing death, of death in battle, 5.83, al

πορφυρίων.definition: purple coot or water-hen, Fulica; a kind of polypus, Artem.2.14

πορφύρω.definition: poet. Verb, only pres. and impf., of the sea, as when the huge sea heaves, surges, swirls with dumb swell , Il.14.16, cf. Arat.158, Artem.2.23; Arat.296; A.R.1.935; of flame, Id.4.668:-later in Med., even in a gently …

ποσαπλάσιος.definition: how many times multiplied?; c.gen., what multiple of . .? ib.84e

ποσθία.definition: foreskin, Ph.2.211; stye on the eyelid, Gal.12.741, Aët.7.84

πόσθων.definition: prop. one with a large; Com. word for a little boy, Ar.Pax1300

ποσσίκλυτος.definition: famed for swiftness of foot, Dionys. ap. St.Byz. s.v

ποτάομαι.definition: poet. Frequentat. of Ep. also; metaph., . . hovers, A.Ag.977 , cf.Ch.390 ; . . Id.Eu.378 , cf. Pers.668 ; to be fluttered, Ar.Av.1445, cf. Nu.319

ποτέχω.definition: Dor. for Ar.Ach.733, etc.; also Ep.aor. part. A.R.3.150

ποτηροθήκη.definition: table for setting out cups, sideboard, buffet, Gloss

πρασιά.definition: Ion. bed in a garden, garden-; a surgical instrument, Hermes 38.283

πράσσω.definition: Ep. and Ion. Att. (first in; in Ep. only, pass through, pass over, Od.9.491; Il.14.282, 23.501; Od.13.83; h.Merc.203: c. gen., Il.24.264, Od.15.219; ib.47; 3.476: Gramm. note that this sense is found only in pres., An…

πρατόπαις.definition: Dor. for at Sparta, in pl., boys in their first year, prob. in ib.5.213.36

πράϋνσις.definition: Ion. softening, appeasing, Arist.Rh.1380a8: Medic., relief, Aret.CA2.11

πρέμνον.definition: bottom of the trunk of a tree, stump; enlarged bark of the stem of the olive, Thphr.HP1.8.6

πρέπω.definition: impf. which were the tenses chiefly in; on the eye, to be clearly seen, to be conspicuous among a number, Il.12.104; Od.8.172, Hes.Th.92; to be distinguished in or by a thing, A.Ch.12, cf. Th.124 , E.Alc.512, 1050; A.…

πρέσβα.definition: Ep. fem. of august, honoured ; in Il. mostly of Hera, 5.721, 8.383, al.; 19.91; later, Q.S.13.378; in Od., of a mortal, 3.452

πρεσβεία.definition: age, seniority, right of the elder; rank, dignity, Pl.R.509b

πρέσβος.definition: poet. word, object of reverence, to them, A.Pers.623 ; august assembly of . . , Id.Ag.855,1393

πρήθω.definition: spout, he spouted blood from his mouth and nostrils, Il.16.350

πρημονάω.definition: perh. fume, seethe or swell with indignation, Herod.6.8

πριόω.definition: = only in 3sg. subj. Tab.Heracl.1.129; pf. part. Pass. Hp.VC20; cf

πρῖσις.definition: sawing, Arist.PA645b17; in cranial surgery, trephining, Hp.VC9, 21

πρίσμα.definition: anything sawn, sawdust; wound resulting from trephining with a saw, Hp.Morb.2.15

πρίω.definition: in surgery, trephine, Hp.VC12, al., Epid.II.cc; pf. part. Pass. serrated, Dsc.4.65

προανακρίνω.definition: examine beforehand, of measures to; inquire beforehand of, Phld.Vit.p.29 J

προανέχω.definition: hold up before, has; intr., rise up above or jut out beyond, Th.7.34: c. gen., J.BJ5.4.4, etc

προανθέω.definition: flower before its season, Thphr.CP1.10.2; flower before leaves appear, Thphr.HP7.13.7

προαυδάω.definition: declare before or first, inf. contr. Ar.Av.556

προαυλέω.definition: play a prelude on the flute, Arist.Rh.1414b23

προβαίνω.definition: fut. pf. aor. 2; of hair, grow, Lib.Or.64.50

προβάλλω.definition: fut. pf. Ep.aor.2; put forward, Pl.Sph.261a; of a horse, Arist.Po.1460b19 ; Paus.4.18.6; Luc.Cat.25: metaph., Men.572:—Pass., v. infr. B.III.1

προβάφιον.definition: substance used in first stage of alloying, Zos.Alch.p.193 B., Maria ap.eund.p.212 B

προβιβάζω.definition: fut. D.C.58.23, Att; push forward, advance, D.S.4.78; exalt, Plb.9.10.4; promote him, D.C.l.c.; Phld. Rh.1.40 S

πρόβλητος.definition: thrown forth or away, cast to; spread, beaten out into plates, prob.l.in LXXJe.10.5

προβλώσκω.definition: aor. inf. go or come forth, go out of the house, Od.19.25; 4.22, cf.24.388, Il.21.37; Od.21.239, cf.Opp.H.2.252: c.gen., Orph.Fr.270.6

προβοάω.definition: shout before, cry aloud, Il.12.277, cf. S.Ph.218

προβολεύς.definition: producer, originator, Procl.in Cra.p.2 P., Gloss

προβολή.definition: putting forward, esp. of a; putting forth, Gp.5.25.1

προβουλή.definition: forethought, of malice; standing committee, dub. in BCH26.168

προβύω.definition: fut. push up the wick of a lamp, trim it, cj.in Ar.V.250: metaph., Com.Adesp.644

προγαμέω.definition: live with a woman before marriage; marry first or before, Ph.2.304, Plu.Alex.70

πρόγαμος.definition: betrothed, Tryph.341; before a marriage: title of a play by Menander, Stob.1.7.2

προγελάω.definition: smile before: metaph. of early morning, Ph.1.603

προγίγνομαι.definition: Ion. and later fut; to be born before, exist before, . . . . Hdt.7.3; Id.2.146; former men, X.Mem.4.8.10; Id.Cyr.8.7.24, etc.; the previous crews, Plb.10.17.12

προδηλόω.definition: make clear beforehand, show plainly; give instructions beforehand, c. inf., Parth.17.3

πρόδοσις.definition: payment beforehand, money advanced; to drink on credit, Hermipp.83

προδότης.definition: Dor. betrayer, traitor; one who abandons in danger, A.Pr.1068 ; And.2.26

προδρομή.definition: running forward: sally, sudden attack, X.An.4.7.10: metaph., your lively sallies, Pl.Alc.1.114a

προέδρα.definition: front seat in a theatre, IG5.113; = principatus, Gloss

προεδρεύω.definition: to be act as president; sit in the front row in the theatre, Luc.JTr.8,11

προεέργω.definition: Ep. for hinder or stop by standing before, c.acc. et inf., Il.11.569

πρόειμι.definition: go forward, advance; of Time, as time went on, Id.3.96; Id.6.129, X.Cyr.8.4.13: Id.An.2.2.19; Pl.Phdr.279a, Tht.150d; Id.Phdr.238d, Prt.339c; the current year, BGU 1126.6 : Hermog.Prog.9

προεισάγω.definition: bring in, introduce before (sc; intr., go on the stage before oneself, Arist.Pol.1336b29

προεισδέω.definition: involve in previous ties: persons bound by previous alliances, Plb.9.31.1

προεκθέω.definition: run out before, sally from the ranks, rush; metaph., outrun, Plu.2.446d; Ael.NA13.11

προεμβάτης.definition: one who first boards the enemy's ship, ibid

προένειμι.definition: to be in before, Malch.p.413 D.; of one already interred in a grave, BCH23.167

προεξιόω.definition: free from impurities, refine, Zos.Alch.p.161 B.:—Pass., PHolm.4.24

προερύω.definition: Ep. aor. , draw on or; drew the swift ship forward, by hauling her from the beach to the sea, Il.1.308; 9.358

προέχω.definition: contr. as always in Hom., exc. Od.12.11; metaph. in Med., put forward as a pretext, S.Ant.80; the cancellation of which is the chief consideration in return for which they pretend that war would not occur, Th.1.140

προέψω.definition: cook or dress before, Hp.Morb.3.17, Dsc.5.11; boil water first, Ruf.Fr.66

προζωννύω.definition: = procingo, Gloss.:—Med. gird oneself in front, as with an apron, Pherecr.62

προήγορος.definition: one who speaks in behalf of; Dor. a magistrate at Catana, Cic. Verr.4.23.50

προθέω.definition: run before, Il.10.362; he; c. acc., outrun, outstrip, X.Cyn.3.7

προθρῴσκω.definition: spring forth or forward, Hom. only in Il. and always in aor. part. 17.522; springing far forward, 14.363; A.R.4.641

πρόθυρον.definition: front-door, door-way, esp. of the; porch, portico, Cratin.42, cf. Dicaearch.Hist.59.8

προϊάπτω.definition: send forth, hurl away to the nether; Pass., project, Nic.Th.723

προΐημι.definition: 3 pres. Il.2.752; 3sg. subj; dismiss, let go, Il.4.398; let her go to the god, i.e. in reverence to him, 1.127

προΐσχω.definition: = hold before, hold out, of boys; = B.I, Hp.Art.30, Mochl.4

προκαθίζω.definition: Ion. perch, of birds, Il.2.463; sit in public, sit in state, Hdt.1.14, cf. 97; Hdn.1.9.3:—Med., Hdt.5.12

προκαίω.definition: burn before, in Pass., to be lighted before, of fires, f.l. in X.An.7.2.18; to be burnt first, aor.subj. Aët.15.14

προκαλέω.definition: call forth, D.C.44.34:—Pass., Plb.22.9.2; to; invite or summon, Hdt.4.201, Th.3.34; Id.4.19; Id.5.43; D.21.226; Pl.Smp.217c; entice them out, Arist.HA534a17; endeavour to attach them to oneself, Plb.3.77.7

προκαλίζομαι.definition: Ep. only pres. and impf., call forth, challenge, defy, Il.5.807, cf. 7.150; 3.19; 4.389; Od.8.228; challenge me not to a pugilistic combat, 18.20

προκάμνω.definition: work or toil before, Thgn.925; toil for or in defence of, S.Aj.1270

προκατέχω.definition: hold or gain possession of beforehand; Pass., to be predetermined, Diogenian.Epicur.3.60

πρόκειμαι.definition: used as Pass. of to be set before; lie exposed, Hdt.1.111; of a tuft of wool, S.Tr.702; says Ajax of himself, Id.Aj.427 , cf. E.Tr.1179; D.43.83; esp. lie dead, A.Th.964 , S.Aj.1059; laid out for burial, E.Alc.1012, c…

πρόκλησις.definition: Ion. calling forth, challenge; sounding of the advance, opp. J.BJ2.20.7

πρόκοιτος.definition: one who keeps watch before a

προκρίνω.definition: choose before others, prefer, select; make a preliminary selection of candidates for office, Arist.Ath.8.1, al.:—Pass., D.57.46, cf. 47, 62

προκυλίνδομαι.definition: Pass., roll forward, of the sea; = foreg., roll at the feet of, Arat.188: fut. App.Ital.5.4: late pres. D.H.8.39; Onos.14.3

προλάμπω.definition: shine forth, Chor.p.164 B; trans., cause to shine forth, Procl.in Prm.p.472 S.; Hierocl.in CA25p.477M

προλέγω.definition: pick out, choose, prefer; foretell, Aeol. aor. part. Alc.Supp.22.7; predict, of an oracle, Hdt.1.53, 8.136; A.Pr.1071 , cf. S.OT973; of a physician, v.l. in Hp.Prog.15; Pl.Euthphr.3c, cf. D.19.298

προλείπω.definition: forsake, abandon, Il.17.275; omit to do a thing, c. inf., S.El.132 ; fall into arrears of rent, BGU197.15

πρόλογος.definition: in early Trag. and Com., prologue of a; one who speaks the prologue, Luc.Pseudol.4

προμάλαξις.definition: previous softening, Ps.-Democr. ap. Zos. Alch.p.161 B

προμαχίζω.definition: fight before, in front of the; fight as champion with another, Il.20.376

προμάχομαι.definition: fight before, fight in the front rank; fight for or in defence of, Ar.V.957

πρόμαχος.definition: fighting before or in front; as Adj., the champion spear, i.e. of Heracles , S.Tr.856

προμηθής.definition: Dor. forethinking, provident; of things, requiring forethought, Hp.Acut.13

προνέμω.definition: assign beforehand, Pi.I.8.18; Med., go forward in grazing: hence, gain ground, spread, S.El.1384

προνέω.definition: heap up before, App.BC4.80; swim before, Ael.NA2.6

προνοέω.definition: perceive before, foresee, Il.18.526, cf; preconceive, Porph.Sent.26

προνομεία.definition: going out to forage or plunder, Plb.4.68.3 : rejected by Thom.Mag.p.275 R

προνόμιον.definition: song sung before the; = earnest-money, Luc.Rh.Pr.17

προξυράω.definition: shave beforehand, Heraclid.Tar. ap. Gal.12.402, Crito ib.484, Alex.Trall.1.1

προοργάζω.definition: prepare beforehand as for reception of a dye, metaph., Dam.Pr.427

προορμάω.definition: in Pass., move forward, push on; intr. in Act., advance, ib.1.4.21, HG5.2.28; of plants, advance, Thphr.CP1.12.8, cf. 1.10.7, etc.:—Pass., ib.1.12.6

προπέμπω.definition: aor. contr. send; with a thing for the object, S.El.1155; afford, furnish, Id.Ph.1205 ; cause, Id.Ant.1287

προπέσσω.definition: Att. digest or concoct beforehand, Gal.UP7.9:— pf. Pass. ib.14.10; inf. Aret.CD1.3

προπίπτω.definition: fut. aor. or throw; rush forward, rush headlong, S.OC157 ; Theoc.24.113; burst forth, Str.16.2.44

προπλέκω.definition: wind, apply a bandage before, aor. part. Pass. Heliod. ap. Orib.48.43.1

προποδέω.definition: perh. walk in front as a guide, Call.Fr.1.2P

προποδίζω.definition: advance the foot; metaph., advance, progress, Dam.Pr.56; ib.57

προπολέω.definition: = foreg., Apollon.Lex. s.v. cj. in; Med., speak like a prophetess, Ach.Tat.4.15

προπότης.definition: one who drinks healths, bands of revellers, E.Rh.361

προπροκυλίνδομαι.definition: Pass., keep rolling before another, roll at his feet, c. gen., Il.22.221; wandering from place to place, Od.17.525

προρέω.definition: Ep. Verb, flow forward or forth, flow amain, of; trans., pour forth, h.Ap.380; A.R.3.225, cf. Orph.A.1132

προσάγω.definition: aor. 2 for aor. 1 v; put to, add, Hdt.9.92; of exercises and food, Hp.Insomn.89; cf. II.5

προσαίρω.definition: raise to a higher level, Philostr.VS2.5.3; is prob. f. l. for they took part, in D.C.43.17

προσαλείφω.definition: rub or smear upon; besmear, Plu.2.559f:—Pass., ib.911e

προσαμύνω.definition: come to aid, Il.2.238, cf. 5.139, 16.509, Plu.Them.9, al

προσάπτω.definition: Ep. fasten to or upon; attach to, bestow upon, grant, Il.24.110; Pi.N.8.37; S.El.356; . . E.Med.1382; Pl.Sph.231a, Lg.822b; Id.R.420d; . . . . Id.Cra.410a; D.61.53; in bad sense, fix upon, attach, . . S.OC236 ; Men.10…

προσαραρίσκω.definition: fit to: pf. 2 Ion. intr., to be fitted to, tires firmly fitted, Il.5.725; X.HG4.7.6: Ep. pf. Pass., Hes.Op.431

προσάσσω.definition: only aor. Med., stored up food for many years in advance, Hdt.1.190, cf. 8.20 ; cf. I.2

προσαυδάω.definition: speak to, address, accost, freq. with a; c. acc. rei, Il.4.203, al.: c. dupl. acc., speak so and so to one, 1.201, 22.37; 17.431

προσβαίνω.definition: Dor. Sophr. in Stud.Ital.10.123; mount, ascend, Hdt.1.84, cf. Plb.7.17.4; Id.1.30.10, etc.; climb up a mountain, of a town, Philostr.VA2.9; PPetr.2p.22

προσβάλλω.definition: Ep. Dor. strike; Math., draw a straight line to meet, c. acc., Archim.Spir.6, al

προσβοάω.definition: = acclamo, Gloss.:—Med., call to oneself, call in, Hdt.6.35

προσδέρκομαι.definition: Ep. Il.16.10, Od.17.518; look closely, S.OC121

προσδέχομαι.definition: Ion. used by Hom. only in Ep; admit, Th.2.12; admit into one's presence, of a king, X.Cyr.7.5.37, HG1.5.9; of a demos receiving foreign emissaries, SIG561.7

προσδέω.definition: c. acc. only, attach, Hdt.2.36; Id.4.195; need besides, c. gen. rei

προσειλέω.definition: Ep. press or force towards, . . Il.10.347; E.Hel.445:—Pass., to be confined, cooped up, S.E.M.9.3, etc

πρόσειμι.definition: inf. used in Att. as fut; come over to the side of, in war, Th.4.85, cf. 1.39

προσεμφύω.definition: implant in addition, Phld.Ir.p.50 W.:—Pass., cling yet more closely, D.S.10.18

προσεπάγω.definition: bring besides, add; in Pass., to be brought before a tribunal, PLips.64.58

προσερεύγομαι.definition: belch at: metaph., break foaming against the rock, Il.15.621 : later

προσθακέω.definition: sit at or near, sit here in suppliant guise, S.OC1166

προσθέω.definition: run towards or to, Th.4.33 , X.Cyr.5.3.20, etc.; Polyaen.5.8.1: abs., X.An.5.7.21

προσιδρύω.definition: place near, Procl.in; Pass., to be installed in office, of a priestess, IG22.1346.19

προσίκτωρ.definition: one that comes to a temple; Pass., he to whom one comes as a suppliant, protector, of a god, ib.119 codd

πρόσκειμαι.definition: lie beside, cling to, S.Ant.1223; of pessaries, to be applied, remain in place, Hp.Nat.Mul.109, Mul.1.37

προσκλίνω.definition: cause to lean against, place against; close the door, J.AJ5.4.2

πρόσκρισις.definition: accretion, increase, growth by; addictio, judicatio, Gloss

προσμυθέομαι.definition: Ep. address, accost, Od.11.143: also c. dat., . . Theoc.25.66

προσνέμω.definition: allot, assign, dedicate to; drive his flocks to pasture, E.Cyc.36

προσνεύω.definition: incline or bend towards, Plu.Brut.1; have an inclination or tendency, Plot.5.1.6

προσόζω.definition: pf. intr., smell of, be redolent; abs., stink, 3pl. aor. LXXPs.37.6

προσπελάζω.definition: cause to approach, bring near to; apply touch, Marcellin.Puls.130

προσπίπτω.definition: Dor. Archyt.1: fut; simply, run to, Hdt.2.2, X.Cyr.1.4.4

προσπίτνω.definition: poet. for , fall upon a; come in, come upon the scene, Id.Ph.1429

προσπλάζω.definition: beat or knock against, touch, Il.12.285: c. dat., Od.11.583; . . . . Xenoph.28.2

προσρέω.definition: aor. Pass. , flow towards; Med., has losses, Hp.Superf.42

προσστείχω.definition: go or come towards, Od.20.73; S.OC30, cf. 320, OT79

προστατέω.definition: = foreg.: rule over, lord it over; to be president, ; IG14.612

προστέρπω.definition: Ep. delight or please besides, Il.15.401

προστίθημι.definition: Dor. also aor. inf; hand over, deliver to, . . A.Pr.83, cf. h.Merc.129; give her to him as wife, Hdt.6.126; but as a dower, Hyp.Lyc.13; E.Ion1545; Id.Hec.368, cf. IA540; Id.Supp.948; Id.Ph.964; Th.4.86; D.C.52.14; als…

προστρέπω.definition: turn towards, esp. towards a god as a; approach , Pi.N.4.55codd

πρόστυπος.definition: executed in low relief, opp; Subst., of the Cherubim, J.AJ3.6.5

πρόσφημι.definition: mostly 3sg. aor. , speak to, address, Il.1.84, Hes.Sc.77, etc.; in a parody of Homer, Cratin.68: c. dupl. acc., Il.4.401: abs., 13.768, Od.11.565:—also inf. Med., 23.106

προσφιλέω.definition: approach so as to kiss, the kissers, late phrase for the rafters, Eust.1327.1

προσφύω.definition: with fut. and aor. 1, cause to grow to; mostly in Pass., with aor. 2 and pf. Act. and fut. Med., grow to or upon, E.Ba.921, cf. Pl.R.611d, Ti.45a; will accrue, Id.Ep.313d: freq. in Arist. of any after or adventitious …

προσφωνέω.definition: call or speak to, address, pres. first in; call by name, . . A.Supp. l.c.; E.Tr.942; salute him king, Plb.10.38.3, etc

προσχίζω.definition: slit before or in front, Gloss

προσχώρησις.definition: approach, v.l. for in; surrendering, joining, Men.Prot.p.102D

προσψύχω.definition: of wind, blow cold, f.l. in; shiver at or beside, Epigr.Gr.292.5

πρόσω.definition: Ep., Ion., Pi., Trag. (but f.l. for in; too far, Pl.Grg.458b; Id.Smp.176d

προτείνω.definition: stretch out before, hold before; expose to danger, . . S.Aj.1270

προτελέω.definition: pay or expend beforehand; initiate or instruct beforehand, Luc.Rh.Pr.14 ; Aristid.1.97 J

προτέμνω.definition: aor. cut off beforehand; cut off in front, cut short, Od.23.196; prune vines, PLond.1.131.375, al

προτέρω.definition: Adv. further, forwards; of Time, sooner, Call.Dian.72

προτεύχω.definition: in pf. inf. Pass. to have; to be brought to light, A.R.4.84

προτίθημι.definition: throw him to the dogs, Il.24.409; E.El.896; hand over for burial, S.El.1198, cf. 1487

προτίκτω.definition: 2 aor. bring forth prematurely; pf. part. having had a child, Sor.1.4

προτιμία.definition: preferring in honour, high honour, Max.Tyr.2.5; paid to . ., SIG601.17

προτιόσσομαι.definition: Ep. Verb, only pres. and impf., and never; of the mind, forebode, 5.389; 14.219, cf. A.R.1.895, al.; so, prob., from thorough knowledge of thee I divine my fate, Il.22.356, cf. A.R.4.1372

προτίω.definition: fut. prefer in honour, prefer, A.Ag.789 , Eu.546 ; . . . . has deemed the one more worthy of burial, S.Ant.22

προτρέπτης.definition: one who admonishes or exhorts, Olymp.in Alc.p.31 C., Gloss

προτρέπω.definition: urge forwards; used by Hom. only intr. in; later, in Act., urge on, impel, S.El.1193; Isoc.5.123; opp. Arist.EN1113b26: c. acc. pers. et inf., urge on, impel, persuade one to do a thing, Hdt.9.90, S.Ant.270; D.2.3, cf…

προτύπτω.definition: intr., press forward; forge beforehand, A.Ag.132

προφαίνω.definition: poet. 2 aor. Pass. B.5.77:—bring to; show forth by word, indicate or declare, Id.Tr.324; indicated by the oracle, D.21.54; Pl.R.545b

προφέρω.definition: Ep. and Ion. impf. Q.S.4.275; of words, cast reproaches in their teeth, Il.2.251; throw in one's teeth, bring forward, allege, esp. in the way of reproach or objection, 3.64, cf. Hdt.1.3, 8.61, 125, Isoc.4.100; D.21.1…

προφεύγω.definition: Hom. only in aor. flee forwards; c. acc., flee from, shun, avoid, Il.6.502, cf. 7.309; 14.81; Od.11.107; . . 22.325, etc.; avoid debts, Hes.Op.647

προφορά.definition: pronunciation, utterance; 'procession', going forth, Plot.2.9.1; Id.4.3.2

πρόφορος.definition: put forward, Il.Pers.6.2; the fluid in which the foetus floats, discharged before parturition, forewaters, Arist.HA586a30

προφράζω.definition: tell or announce beforehand, Hdt.1.120; Pass., to be explained above or previously, Nicom.Ar.1.19

προφρύγω.definition: toast, parch before, aor. part. Pass. v.l. for in Dsc.2.90

προφυράω.definition: knead beforehand:—Pass; metaph., the speech is all ready concocted, Ar.Av.462; there's a mischief ready brewed for me, Id.Th.75

προχαίρω.definition: rejoice beforehand, Pl.Phlb.39d; far be it from me! away with it! A.Ag.252

πρόχευμα.definition: that which is poured forth, silt, deposit, Arist.PA647b4

προχέω.definition: pour forth or forward, of a river, Il.21.219, cf. h.Ap.241; Pi.P.1.22; pour in three parts of water first, Hes.Op.596; Hdt.7.192; Critias17D.: metaph., Pi.P.10.56, cf.IG3.713.4; Anacreont.41.10:—Pass., pour on or fort…

προχοή.definition: poet. noun, almost always pl; overflow, flood, A.R.4.271

προχορεύω.definition: go or dance before in a chorus, lead a or festive band, E.Ph.791

προχόω.definition: collat. pres. of pile in front, heap up, Pl.Criti.111b , cf. Aristid.1.128J

προχρονέω.definition: precede in time, c. gen., Ptol.Phas.p.8 H., al

προχωννύω.definition: pf. form by deposition before; dam back, Aristid.Or.46.17

πρυμνόν.definition: lower part, end, Il.5.339: pl., at the far end of the agora, Pi.P.5.93.—Prop.neut. of sq

πρωτοδαής.definition: having learnt for the first time, Opp.H.4.323

πρωτόζυγον.definition: front rank of a squad of cavalry, Afric.Cest.p.58 V

πταίρω.definition: Hippiatr.38 , also Hdn. Gr.1.191 codd. , impf. Diog.Ep.35.3): aor. 2 Od.17.541, etc.: rarely aor. 1, part. Arist.Pr.963a33 :—Pass., v. sub fin.:—sneeze, he sneezed aloud, Od. l.c. ; but also as a bad omen, Men.534.9; …

πτερόω.definition: furnish with feathers or wings; represent as winged, Porph.Abst.3.16

πτερύγισμα.definition: flapping of the wings, cj. for in Longin.Proll.Heph.p.83 C. ; cj. Nauck

πτέρωμα.definition: that which is feathered, e.g; the fin by the gills of fishes, Ael.NA16.12

πτέρων.definition: a bird of some kind, Com.Adesp.592

πτήσσω.definition: Causal, scare, alarm, Il.14.40; Thgn.1015; crouch, of men in ambush, Id.Andr.753; Od.14.474

πτίλος.definition: suffering from II, LXXLe.21.20; alone, Gal.10.1017, 12.799; also Dsc.1.69.3: = lippus, Gloss

πτιλόω.definition: furnish with feathers, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69:—Pass., to have wings, Philostr.VA3.48

πτίλωσις.definition: a disease of the eyelids in which their edges become swollen and inflamed, and the eyelashes fall off, Gal.10.1004, Aët.7.80

πτιλώσσω.definition: have sore eyes, Archyt. ap. Simp.in Cat.395.35

πτισάνης.definition: Dor. one who shells or peels, dub.l. in AP11.351.6 ; Scaliger

πτοέω.definition: and fut. AP7.214 : Ep. aor; metaph., flutter, excite by any passion, . . Sapph.2.6, cf. eand.Supp.14.6; A.R.1.1232; Poet. ap.Parth.21.2:—Pass., to be passionately excited, Mimn.5.2 ; A.Pr.856; E.Ba.214, cf. IA1029; ib…

πτολίοικος.definition: dweller in the city, on Cretan coins, BMus.Cat.Coins Crete p.8

πτόρθος.definition: young branch, shoot, sucker, sapling; sprouting, budding, Hes.Op.421

πτύσσω.definition: Pass., of the foetus, Hp.Mul.1.69; of bandages, Gal.18.826; Hdn.1.17.1; App. l.c.; perh. were interlaced, Il. l.c

πτύω.definition: Il.23.697, etc.: fut. Hp.Prorrh.2.40; of the sea, disgorge, cast out, . . . . AP7.283 , cf. Opp.H.5.596: metaph., AP7.468 : abs., of waves, Theoc.15.133; with a splash, AP9.290

πτωματίς.definition: tumbler, i.e. cup that will not stand upright, and therefore must be emptied at once, Mosch. ap. Ath.11.485e

πτωσκάζω.definition: poet. for sq., crouch or cower for fear, Il.4.372

πτώσσω.definition: only pres., shrink from, shrink, of birds or; cringe like a beggar, go begging , Od.17.227, 18.363: c. acc. loci, Hes.Op.395

πτωχεία.definition: Ion. beggary, mendicity; poor relief, Cod.Just.1.3.41.23

πτωχεύω.definition: fut. Od.15.309: Ep. impf; to be as poor as a beggar, Antiph.322, Pl.Erx.394b

πυγαλγίας.definition: suffering pain in the buttocks, Democles Pygelensis ap. Str.14.1.20

πυγεών.definition: dub. sens. in Hippon. in PSI9.1089.2

πυγή.definition: heterocl. acc. Arist.Phgn.810b1; metaph. of fat, swelling land, Eust.310.2

πυγοσκελίς.definition: waterbird with legs set far back, like the grebe or puffin, Id

πυέλιον.definition: Dim. of prov., 'when pigs begin to fly', Diogenian.3.7

πυελίς.definition: in a seal-ring, setting, socket of; bearing or axle-box, HeroAut.5.3, Apollod.Poliorc.148.8

πυθιάζω.definition: to be inspired by Apollo, prophesy, St.Byz. s.v

πυθμενέω.definition: of a number, to be a base of a series, prob. in Iamb.in Nic.p.117 P

πύθω.definition: Ep. impf. A.R.4.1530: fut. Il.4.174: aor. h.Ap.371, Ep. ib.374 : -Pass., only used in pres. and impf.:-cause to rot, Il.4.174; h.Ap.369; ib.374, cf. Hes.Op.626:-Pass., become rotten, decay, moulder, Il.11.395; Od.1.16…

πυκάζω.definition: Od.12.225, Dor. Theoc.3.14: impf; metaph., threw a shadow over his soul, Il.8.124, 17.83:—Pass., Epigr.Gr.875.2 ; also close, cautious of mind, Hes.Op.793

πύκασμα.definition: that which is close, covered, or thick, Sm.Ps.117.27

πυκνίτης.definition: assembled in the Pnyx, Ar.Eq.42: fem. from the Pnyx, IG22.1672.199

πυλουρός.definition: = Hdt.3.72,77,118,140,156 , Baur and Rostovtzeff Second Report on Dura-Europos138 , Gloss.: as fem., ib

πυλόω.definition: furnish with gates, X.HG5.4.34:—Pass., to be so furnished, Ar.Av.1158

πυνθάνομαι.definition: Od.2.315, etc.; poet. also; c. acc. rei only, hear or learn a thing, Od.2.411, A.Ch.765, Antipho5.25, etc.: abs., Il.2.119, cf. Pi.P.7.7, etc.; Hdt.1.22, etc

πυξίζω.definition: to be yellow like box-wood, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.63

πυξίον.definition: tablet of box-wood for painting on; list, hence section, division, JudeichAltertümer von HierapolisNo. 278.3, cf. 209.7 , 234.4

πυξίς.definition: box of box-wood: generally, box (cf; cylinder in which a piston works, HeroSpir.1.28

πυόω.definition: cause to suppurate, Eust.464.27:—Pass., suppurate, Arist.Resp.479b30

πυράζω.definition: singe, coined as etym. of EM697.16

πυρακτέω.definition: turn in the fire: hence, harden in the; burn, Nic.Th.688

πυργόω.definition: gird or fence with towers; metaph., fence, protect, Nonn.D.30.52, etc

πυρεύς.definition: one who lights fire or burns; fire-proof vessel, cj. in AP13.13

πυρήφατος.definition: formed like wheat-pounding servant of Demeter, i.e. a millstone, AP7.394

πυρία.definition: Ion. vapour-bath, made by; generally of all forms of external application of heat, Hp.Acut.21; Gal.15.519, cf. Hp.Aph.5.28, 6.31; of cauteries, Aret.CD1.2

πυριάω.definition: Ion. inf. Hp.Nat.Mul.107, but; c. dupl. acc., Hp.Mul.1.75

πυριμανέω.definition: break out into a furious blaze, Plu.Alex.35

πυρόω.definition: burn with fire, burn up; seem hot to the taste or tongue, Dsc.1.16, 4.170

πυρπολέω.definition: light and keep up a fire, watch a fire; burn with fire, Id.Th.727; of the bull of Phalaris, Phalar.Ep.66.2:—Pass., Phld.Piet.89

πυρράζω.definition: to be fiery red, of the sky, Ev.Matt.16.2

πυρριάω.definition: to be or become red: blush, Ach.Tat.2.11; to be of a ruddy complexion, Procop.Arc.8

πυρσεύω.definition: light up, kindle; set on fire, Opp.C.1.327

πω.definition: Ion. enclit. Particle, up to this time, yet, in; at all, with neg. in Ep., Il.1.124; 3.306; 15.426: after Hom. sts. with questions which imply a negative, S.OT1130 ; has ever a city meditating revolt . .? Th.3.45

πωλέομαι.definition: Ion. used by Hom. in 2sg. Od.4.811; part. 2.55 : impf. Od.22.352, 9.189; Ion. impf. Il.1.490, Od.11.240: fut. h.Ap.329, Ep. 2sg. Il.5.350:—Ep. Verb, prop. Frequentat. of go up and down or to and fro: hence, go or come…

πωρόω.definition: petrify, Ael.NA10.13; cause a stone or callus to form:—Pass., of a stone forming in the bladder, Hp.Aër.9

πωτάομαι.definition: Ep. impf. Il.12.287: Dor. fut. Ar.Lys.1013: aor. AP7.699, Babr.12.1:—poet. Frequentat. of fly about, Il. l.c.; h.Ap.442; . . Pi.Fr.132.1 ; . . Theoc.7.142; Q.S.5.437; Ion. impf. Orac. ap. Marin.Procl.28

παι.definition: a demonstr. Particle in Cypr., Inscr.Cypr. 135.4 H., al

παμμαχί.definition: Adv. in which all fight, A.D.Conj.234.9

παμπαιδί.definition: Adv. with all their children, D.C.41.9; cf

πάμπαλιν.definition: Adv. altogether to the contrary, Crates Com.15

πάμπαν.definition: Adv., wholly, altogether, with Verb; as Adj., IG12.6.117

πάμπανυ.definition: Adv. strengthd. for dub. in D.C.56.30

πανεθνεί.definition: Adv. with the whole nation, Str.5.1.6:—also LXXWi.19.8

πάνετες.definition: Adv., all the year long, Pi.P.1.20

πανῆμαρ.definition: Adv. all day, the livelong day, Od.13.31

πάρεγγυς.definition: Adv. near at hand, close by; of Time, near, i. e. in age, Id.Pol.1335a1; following closely on . . , Id.GA773b9

παρηγμένως.definition: Adv., redundantly, of a compound word, part of which loses its significance, Apollon.Lex. s.v

πάρος.definition: of Time, aforetime, formerly, Il.4.73, etc.; 22.403; 11.669, cf. Od.2.119, etc.; opp. 6.325, etc. ; Il.17.270, etc. ; Od.5.82, etc. : with the Art., Il.19.42, 23.480, etc. ; once in Hdt., 9.2; never in Att. Prose , PO…

πάτρηθε.definition: and Adv., = from one's; from a family or clan, Dor. Pi.N.7.70

πατριστί.definition: Adv. = OGI46.7 , Bull.Soc. royale des lettres de Lund1928/9iv3

πεδόθεν.definition: Adv., from the ground; from the bottom, Pi.O.7.62: metaph., which are dear to thee from the bottom of thy heart, Od.13.295

πέδοι.definition: Adv. on the ground, on earth, A.Pr.274; cf. 4

πέδονδε.definition: Adv. to the ground, earthwards, Il.13.796; to the bottom, Od.11.598

περ.definition: enclit. Particle, adding force to the word to; in Hom. freq. with Adj. and part. all shortlived as I am, Il.1.352; ib.587; 3.201: mostly concessive like , however brave thou art, 1.131, al.; 15.164; 9.373; ib.343; 5.6…

πέραν.definition: Ion. and Ep. Adv. on the other side; abs., on the other side, esp. of water, . . Hdt.6.97; X.An.2.4.20, 3.5.12, etc.; ib.6.5.22

πετρηδόν.definition: Adv. like stones, of hail, Luc.Tim.3

πη.definition: Dor. Adv. somewhere, anywhere; indirect interrog. where, Supp.Epigr.4.70 ; cf. sq. II.2

πηνίκα.definition: interrog. Adv. correl. to and at; in indirect questions, Men.367

πλεοναχῇ.definition: Adv. from many points of view, Pl.R.477a

πλεύνως.definition: Adv. Ion. for too much, Hdt.5.18

πόθεν.definition: interrog. Adv. whence?; of origin, from what stock he avows that he is by descent, Od.17.373; . . Pl.Phdr.269d; . .; D.3.28: c. gen., . . E.Supp.841

ποῖ.definition: interrog. Adv. whither? v.l. in Thgn.586 (leg; c. gen., to what spot of earth? Id.Supp.777 , S.Tr.984 , etc.; Id.OC170 , 310, Tr.705; cf

πόλεμόνδε.definition: Ep. Adv. into the fight; to the war, Od.11.448

πόλινδε.definition: Adv. into or to the city, Il.5.224, al

ποντόθεν.definition: Adv.from or out of the sea, Il.14.395

ποσάκις.definition: Adv. how many times? how often?; Indef., so many times, i.e. square numbers, and cubes, Arist.Metaph.1020b5

πόσε.definition: Adv. whither? Il.16.422, Od.6.199; 10.431:—Ep. for later

ποσίνδα.definition: Adv., how many times? = play morra, X.Eq.Mag.5.10

ποσσῆμαρ.definition: Adv. for how many days? Il.24.657

ποτέρωθεν.definition: Adv., from which of two quarters, Arist.Mete.361a25

ποτέρωθι.definition: Adv. on whether of the two sides? on which side ? Pl.Phdr.263b; Answ. X.Mem.4.2.17

ποτέρως.definition: Adv. of in which of two ways?; in indirect questions, Pl.R.341b; . . ib.368c, cf.Plt.272d

ποτέρωσε.definition: Adv. to which of two sides? Answ. X.Mem.4.2.14; Orph.Fr.135

ποῦ.definition: Ion. interrog. Adv. where? Hom., etc.; freq; so in a sense not strictly local, S.El.390; Id.Ant.42; Id.Tr.375; at what point of fortune stands he? Id.Aj.102

πρίν.definition: Adv. and Conj., before, until. 19 times in; of future time, with fut. Indic., Il.1.29, cf. 18.283, Od.2.198, etc.: with Subj. = fut., Il.24.551: with Opt. and Od.3.117, cf. 11.330, 14.155, Ar.Pax1076, 1112: with Opt.,…

πρόκα.definition: Ion. Adv. forthwith, straightway, Hp. ap. Gal.19.132, A.R.1.688; in Hdt. or 1.111, 6.134, 8.65, 135; so also in Call. in PSI19.1092.52

προμηκικῶς.definition: Adv. by the use of unequal factors , Iamb.in Nic.p.89 P

προνύξ.definition: Adv. all night long, opp. Semon.7.47

πρόπαρ.definition: Prep. with gen., before, in front of; abs. as Adv., before, sooner, rather, A.Supp.791

προπρό.definition: strengthd. for Prep. with gen., before; Adv. on and on, thoroughly, ib.1013,4.1235, Euph.94. More freq. in compds., v. infr

πρόπρυμνα.definition: Adv. away from the stern, of jettisoning cargo, metaph. in A.Th.769

πρός.definition: Prep., expressing direction, on the side of, in; on the side of, towards, towards Elis, Od.21.347; Il.10.428,430; Hdt.2.154; Id.8.120; Th.1.62, etc.; on the frontier towards the Ethiopians, etc., Hdt.2.30: freq. with …

προσεπί.definition: Prep. c. dat., in addition to, PSI4.298.13 , PMasp.243.18 , etc

πρόχνυ.definition: with the knees forward, i.e. kneeling or crouching, Il.9.570 )

πυγηδόν.definition: Adv. tail foremost, of; rump to rump, Id.HA539b22

πυκινά.definition: neut. pl. used as Adv., v. B.II

πυκνά.definition: neut. used as Adv., v. B.II

πῶς.definition: Ion. interrog. Adv. of Manner, how? Il.1.123; in dialogue, to ask explanation, with a repetition of a word used by the previous speaker, Answ. S.OC832; Id.Tr.412; Alex.143; alone, how so, . . ; S.Ph.1386

πως.definition: Ion. enclit. Adv. of Manner, in any way, at; or in a certain way, opp. Arist.Pol.1275a16; Id.EN1106a1; ib.1137a12

περικείρω.definition: aor. inf. Philostr.Ep.61: pf; metaph., shear of its walls, Ael.VH7.8

πολύβροχος.definition: freshly infused several times, Dsc.1.128.6, al; with many nooses, E.HF1035

προσυνάγω.definition: arrive at a total beforehand:—Pass., Vett.Val.32.3

παρανατολή.definition: simultaneous rising, in pl., Eudem. ap. Theon.Sm.p.200 H., Cat.Cod.Astr.8.207

πεζομαχία.definition: Ion. battle by land, opp; fighting on foot, opp. Ph.1.191 , cf. Arr.An.1.15.4

ποιφύσσω.definition: trans., blow up, Lyc.198; puff out, AP7.215

παράδρομος.definition: that may be run through, spaces; running alongside, Stad.67

πρόσκρουσις.definition: dashing against a thing; offence, give him offence, Id.Cic.34, cf. 2.138e , etc

πρημνάς.definition: a kind of tunny-fish, Pl.Com.44, Nicoch.11 , Opp.H.1.183; and in codd. of Arist.HA599b17

πόθι.definition: interrog. Adv., poet. for where? Od.1.170; later for whither? A.R.1.242, AP7.566 . B. enclit. Adv., poet. for anywhere, somewhere, Il.10.8, etc.; S.Aj.886

πεντάμηνος.definition: five months old, Arist.HA568a12; consisting of five months, Plu.2.933e

προανεγείρω.definition: arouse, awaken beforehand, Procl.in Prm.p.606S., cf. Syrian.in Metaph.149.12

παρεκφέρω.definition: abuse, prob. in; to be excreted with, Aët.5.28

πάμψυχος.definition: in full life, of Amphiaraus, S.El.841

παππίας.definition: Dim. of dear little papa, a term of endearment, Ar.V.297, Pax128, Ephipp.21

πλατύσημος.definition: with broad border, =; of those entitled to wear it, = tribunus laticlavius, IG4.588.4 , IGRom.3.554 , 889

περιζώστρα.definition: apron, Anaxandr.69; ribbon twined round a garland, dub. in Theoc.2.122

προαναφέρω.definition: bring up or mention before, v.l. in; Pass., rush up before, Arist.Pr.897a28

πτέρωσις.definition: feathering of arrows, Aen. Tact.31.27; metaph., Jul.Ep.193

προσαναρτάω.definition: hang upon, Luc.Philops.11: metaph., attach, connect, in Pass., Phld.Ir.p.80 W

περιτρυπάω.definition: perforate with a circle of holes, Aët.9.38, Paul.Aeg.6.3

προπληρόω.definition: fill before, Asclep. ap. Gal.12.586, Ph.1.603, Dsc.Alex. Praef

ποσσίκροτος.definition: struck with the foot in dancing; Act., striking with the feet, Orph.H.31.2

πυρφορέω.definition: to be a torch-bearer, E.Tr.348: c. acc; esp. to be a or bearer of sacred fire, IG7.1776 ; ib.42.121.43

ποταμηπόρος.definition: crossing rivers, Opp.C.2.178; going to the river, ib.4.84

παρακλιδόν.definition: Adv., turning aside; leaning against, Orph.A.559

περίπικρος.definition: very harsh or bitter, Phld.Ir.p.6 W., Ptol.Tetr.160, Procl.Par.Ptol.225

πωλοτρόφος.definition: rearing young horses; generally, their trainers, Ael.NA16.36

πολυσιτία.definition: abundance of corn or food, X.HG5.2.16; much eating, Luc.Par.16

πενθητήρ.definition: mourner, A.Pers.946 , Th.1067 :—fem. she who mourns for, E.Hipp.805

περιρρώξ.definition: broken off all round, abrupt, Plb.9.27.4, cf. D.H.9.15

πατητήριον.definition: place where grapes are trodden, CIG2694a10 , Androtion or Philippus ap.Harp. s.v

πανημέριος.definition: Dor. all day long; of the whole day, the livelong day, E.Hipp.369

πύρινος.definition: metaph., bitter, obstinate war, Plb.35.1.6, D.S.31.40; fiery greeting, PMag.Par.1.638

παραφθαδόν.definition: Adv. overtaking, c. gen., Opp.H.3.298: abs., in rivalry, ib.4.97

πήχυιος.definition: = A.R.3.1207; 'but a span', Mimn.2.3; projecting for the space of a cubit, A.R.1.379

πλυντρίς.definition: a kind of fuller's earth, Menestor ap. Thphr.CP2.4.3, Nicoch.4
